head: Ἕλενος
text: Helenus, son of Priam and Hecuba, a seer. Captured by the Greeks, he foretells that Troy will fall only with Philoctetes and his bow; later he marries Andromache.

head: Ἕλλη
text: Helle, daughter of Athamas and Nephele and sister of Phrixus. Fleeing on the golden ram, she fell into the sea, named after her the Hellespont, "Helle's sea".

head: Ἕρμιππος
text: Hermippus, an Athenian poet of Old Comedy, older than Aristophanes, who attacked Pericles and Hyperbolus.

head: Ἵππυλλος
text: Hippyllus, one of the guests at the drinking party in Wasps where Philocleon gets drunk.

head: Ἵππωναξ
text: Hipponax of Ephesus, an iambic poet of the 500s BC known for biting satire; Dionysus in Frogs quotes a line of his.

head: Ἁλιμοῦς
text: Halimus, an Attic deme near the coast, the deme of Thucydides the historian.

head: Ἑκάβη
text: Hecuba, wife of Priam, king of Troy, and mother of Hector, Paris, Cassandra, and Polyxena. After the fall of Troy she is a slave of the Greeks; she leads Euripides' Hecuba and Trojan Women.

head: Ἑκάτειον
text: a Hecateion, a small shrine or image of Hecate set at doors and crossroads.

head: Ἑλικωνιάδες
text: the Heliconian ones, the Muses or nymphs of Helicon, the mountain in Boeotia that was the Muses' favourite haunt.

head: Ἑρμιόνη
text: Hermione, the only daughter of Menelaus and Helen. In Andromache she is Neoptolemus' jealous Spartan wife and leaves with Orestes; in Orestes he holds her hostage.

head: Ἑρμιών
text: Hermion or Hermione, a town on the southeast coast of Argolis.

head: Ἡγέλοχος
text: Hegelochus, the Athenian actor who played Euripides' Orestes and mispronounced one word, so that the line said "a weasel" for "calm"; the comic poets never let him forget it.

head: Ἡρακλειοξανθίας
text: Heracleoxanthias, a joke compound in Frogs: Xanthias dressed up as Heracles.

head: Ἡσιόνη
text: Hesione, a daughter of Ocean whom Prometheus married; the chorus of Ocean's daughters sang at the wedding.

head: Ἱεροκλέης
text: Hierocles, the oracle-monger from Oreus in Euboea who tries to stop the peace sacrifice in Peace and is driven off.

head: Ἱππόκινος
text: Hippocinus, a pun on Hipponicus: Callias, 'son of Hippocinus' ('horse-fucker'), mocked in Frogs.

head: Ἱπποδάμεια
text: Hippodameia, daughter of Oenomaus, king of Pisa. Pelops won her by killing her father in a chariot race.

head: Ἱσμήνη
text: Ismene, daughter of Oedipus and Jocasta, sister of Antigone, Eteocles, and Polynices.

head: Ἱσμηνός
text: Ismenus, the river of Thebes, which flows past the city near the spring Dirce.

head: Ὁμόλη
text: Homole, a mountain of Thessaly by the vale of Tempe, part of Ossa; in Heracles a haunt of the Centaurs.

head: Ῥαδαμάνθυς
text: Rhadamanthys, son of Zeus and Europa, brother of Minos; for his justice made a judge in the world of the dead.

head: Ῥοδίππη
text: Rhodippe, one of the old women of the chorus in Lysistrata.

head: Ὑπέρβολος
text: Hyperbolus, an Athenian demagogue who rose to lead the people after Cleon. A lamp-maker by trade, he is mocked by Aristophanes as a low-born rogue; he was later ostracised.

head: Ὑσιαί
text: Hysiae, a town of Boeotia at the foot of Mount Cithaeron, which the Theban bacchants raid.

head: Ὑσταίχμας
text: Hystaechmas, a Persian lord named among the lost in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Ἄβαι
text: Abae, a town of Phocis with an old oracle of Apollo.

head: Ἄλκηστις
text: Alcestis, daughter of Pelias and wife of Admetus, king of Pherae, who dies in her husband's place; Heracles wrestles Death and brings her back in Euripides' Alcestis.

head: Ἄλπιστος
text: Alpistus, son of Batanochus, a Persian named among the lost in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Ἄμφιων
text: Amphion, son of Zeus and Antiope and twin of Zethus. He built the walls of Thebes, the stones moving to the music of his lyre, and married Niobe; 'the house of Amphion' means Thebes.

head: Ἄμιστρις
text: Amistris, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, killed at Salamis.

head: Ἄνυτος
text: Anytus, son of Anthemion, a leading Athenian politician, later the chief accuser of Socrates.

head: Ἔρυξις
text: Eryxis, son of Philoxenus, an Athenian mocked in Frogs, where Dionysus guesses that a monster in Aeschylus is Eryxis.

head: Ἴβυκος
text: Ibycus of Rhegium, lyric poet of the sixth century BC, named in Thesmophoriazusae with Anacreon and Alcaeus as a poet of soft love songs.

head: Ἴφιτος
text: Iphitus, son of Eurytus of Oechalia, whom Heracles killed by treachery; for that he was sold as a slave to Omphale.

head: Ἴκαρος
text: Icarus, an island of the Aegean west of Samos, named after Daedalus' son, who fell into the sea nearby.

head: Ἴθακος
text: Ithacan, of Ithaca, the island kingdom of Odysseus.

head: Ἦλις
text: Elis, the region and city of the northwest Peloponnese, in which Olympia lies.

head: Ἀβαντίδης
text: of the Abantes, the old people of Euboea; hence Euboean.

head: Ἀβαντίς
text: Abantian, of the Abantes, the old people of Euboea; Ἀβαντίς, Euboea.

head: Ἀδεύης
text: Adeues, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, named among those killed at Salamis.

head: Ἀδμήτειος
text: of Admetus (Ἄδμητος), king of Pherae in Thessaly, husband of Alcestis.

head: Ἀδριανός
text: Adriatic; ἡ Ἀδριανὴ ἀκτή, the shore of the Adriatic sea, where the poplars weep amber for Phaethon.

head: Ἀερόπη
text: Aerope, a Cretan princess, wife of Atreus and mother of Agamemnon and Menelaus. She took Atreus' brother Thyestes as her lover, which began the feud of the house.

head: Ἀγαβάτανα
text: Agabatana, another form of Ἀγβάτανα (Ecbatana), the capital of Media.

head: Ἀγαβάτας
text: Agabatas (or Agdabatas), a Persian named in the lament of Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Ἀγαμεμνόνεος
text: of Agamemnon, Agamemnon's; also spelled Ἀγαμεμνόνιος. παῖς Ἀγαμεμνονία, Agamemnon's daughter (Iphigenia or Electra); Ἀγαμεμνονία ἄλοχος, Agamemnon's wife.

head: Ἀγαμεμνόνιος
text: of Agamemnon, king of Mycenae and leader of the Greeks against Troy. Ἀγαμεμνόνιος κέλωρ or θάλος, the son of Agamemnon, Orestes.

head: Ἀγαμεμνονίδης
text: son of Agamemnon: Orestes.

head: Ἀγβάτανα
text: Agbatana (Ecbatana), the capital of Media and a royal seat of the Persian kings.

head: Ἀγδαδάτας
text: Agdadatas, a Persian lord named among the lost in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Ἀγηνορίδης
text: descendant of Agenor, king of Phoenicia and father of Cadmus; in the plural, Cadmus' line, the royal house of Thebes.

head: Ἀγλαυρίς
text: daughter of Aglauros (Ἄγλαυρος), wife of Cecrops, first king of Athens; αἱ Ἀγλαυρίδες, their daughters.

head: Ἀγοράκριτος
text: Agoracritus ("chosen in the market"), the name the Sausage-seller gives himself at the end of Aristophanes' Knights, once he has beaten Paphlagon.

head: Ἀγύρριος
text: Agyrrhius of Collytus, an Athenian politician who raised the pay for attending the Assembly to three obols in the 390s BC; Aristophanes mocks him in Assemblywomen and Wealth.

head: Ἀκραίη
text: Ionic form of Ἀκραία: Acraea ("of the height"), a title of Hera, whose sanctuary on the heights at Corinth is where Medea buries her children.

head: Ἀλφειός
text: Alpheus, the chief river of the Peloponnese, which flows past Olympia; its banks stand for the Olympic games. Its god loved the nymph Arethusa.

head: Ἀλφεός
text: Alpheus, the chief river of the western Peloponnese, flowing past Olympia, and its river god.

head: Ἀλκάθοος
text: Alcathous, son of Pelops and brother of Atreus and Thyestes, who killed the lion of Cithaeron and became king of Megara; in Children of Heracles "the borders of Alcathous" means Megara.

head: Ἀλκιβιάδης
text: Alcibiades, son of Cleinias, the brilliant Athenian general and politician, in exile when Frogs was staged; the city's love and fear of him is a question in that play.

head: Ἀλκμήνη
text: Alcmene, daughter of Electryon and wife of Amphitryon, mother of Heracles by Zeus. In Children of Heracles she guards her grandchildren and demands Eurystheus' death.

head: Ἀλόπη
text: Alope, daughter of Cercyon, loved by Poseidon; in Birds she is one of the mortal women Zeus was free to visit.

head: Ἀμεινίης
text: Ionic form of Ἀμεινίας: Ameinias (Amynias), an Athenian to whom Strepsiades owes money in Clouds; Socrates also uses the name in his lesson on genders.

head: Ἀμφαναία
text: Amphanaea, a town of northern Greece, home of Cycnus, the robber whom Heracles shot.

head: Ἀμφίονιος
text: of Amphion (Ἀμφίων), son of Zeus and Antiope, whose lyre raised the walls of Thebes.

head: Ἀμφίθεος
text: Amphitheus ("god on both sides"), the comic immortal in Acharnians who claims descent from Demeter and Triptolemus and fetches Dicaeopolis' private peace from Sparta.

head: Ἀμφιστρεύς
text: Amphistreus, a Persian spearman named among the dead at Salamis in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Ἀμφιτρύων
text: Amphitryon, son of Alcaeus and grandson of Perseus, husband of Alcmene and the human father of Heracles. In Euripides' Heracles the old man guards Heracles' wife and sons at Thebes.

head: Ἀμίστρης
text: Amistres, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, named first in the muster of leaders.

head: Ἀμμωνίς
text: of Ammon, the Libyan god whom the Greeks took for Zeus; Ἀμμωνίδες ἕδραι, the seat of Ammon's oracle in the Libyan desert.

head: Ἀμμωνιάς
text: of Ammon, the Libyan god the Greeks called Zeus Ammon, whose oracle stood in the desert.

head: Ἀμυμώνιος
text: of Amymone, daughter of Danaus, to whom Poseidon showed the springs at Lerna; Ἀμυμώνια ὕδατα, the waters of Lerna.

head: Ἀναφλύστιος
text: of Anaphlystus, a deme of Attica on the west coast near Sunium; a man from there. Aristophanes uses it in a sexual pun.

head: Ἀναγυρουντόθεν
text: from Anagyrus, a deme of Attica on the coast south of Athens.

head: Ἀνδροκλέης
text: Androcles, an Athenian demagogue who helped drive Alcibiades into exile in 415 BC.

head: Ἀνθράκυλλος
text: Anthracyllus ('little coal'), a poor Acharnian named as one who never served on a paid embassy.

head: Ἀντίλοχος
text: Antilochus, son of Nestor, a Greek hero at Troy who died there, the grief of his old father.

head: Ἀντιγόνη
text: Antigone, daughter of Oedipus and Jocasta, sister of Eteocles, Polynices, and Ismene. She guides her blind father into exile and buries Polynices against Creon's order, for which she dies.

head: Ἀντισθένης
text: Antisthenes, an Athenian in Assemblywomen whom a man in pain calls for, as one who knows all about groaning.

head: Ἀπιδανός
text: Apidanus, a river of Thessaly that waters the plain of Phthia.

head: Ἀπιόθεν
text: from Apia, an old name of the Peloponnese, hence from Argos.

head: Ἀποδρασιππίδης
text: Apodrasippides ("son of Run-off-horse"), a joke name in Wasps: Philocleon, escaping like Odysseus, calls himself Nobody, son of Apodrasippides.

head: Ἀθάμας
text: Athamas, son of Aeolus, king in Boeotia, husband of Nephele, and father of Phrixus and Helle. In Clouds Strepsiades, crowned, fears he will be sacrificed like Athamas.

head: Ἀθαμαντίς
text: daughter of Athamas: Helle, who fell from the golden ram into the strait named after her, the Hellespont.

head: Ἀθήναζε
text: to Athens (Ἀθῆναι).

head: Ἀθμονεύς
text: of Athmonon, a deme of Attica; Trygaeus, the hero of Peace, is of Athmonon.

head: Ἀργαδεῖς
text: the Argadeis, one of the four old Ionian tribes of Athens; in Ion, Athena says they will take their name from a son of Ion.

head: Ἀργῷος
text: of the Argo, the ship in which Jason and the Argonauts sailed to Colchis for the Golden Fleece.

head: Ἀρίστυλλος
text: Aristyllus, an Athenian mocked by Aristophanes for his filthy sexual habits.

head: Ἀριμασπός
text: Arimaspian: the Arimaspi, a one-eyed Scythian people of the far north who live by a river of gold.

head: Ἀριόμαρδος
text: Ariomardus, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, ruler of Egyptian Thebes, mourned among the dead after Salamis.

head: Ἀριστείδης
text: Aristides, the Athenian statesman of the Persian Wars, called "the Just", recalled with Miltiades as a model of the old Athens.

head: Ἀριστογείτων
text: Aristogeiton, the Athenian who with Harmodius killed Hipparchus, brother of the tyrant Hippias, in 514 BC; Athens honoured both as tyrant-slayers.

head: Ἀριστομάχη
text: Aristomache ('best in battle'), a woman's name the chorus of Thesmophoriazusae sets against the men; 'the one at Marathon' plays on the name.

head: Ἀρκτεύς
text: Arcteus, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, named in the muster and among those killed at Salamis.

head: Ἀρσάκης
text: Arsaces, a Persian cavalry leader whose death Xerxes mourns in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Ἀρσάμης
text: Arsames, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, ruler of Memphis, killed at Salamis.

head: Ἀρταφρένης
text: Artaphrenes (Herodotus' Artaphernes), a Persian noble name. In Persians one commander bears it, and Darius tells how an Artaphrenes killed the usurper Mardus by a trick.

head: Ἀρτεμβάρης
text: Artembares, a Persian cavalry commander in Aeschylus' Persians, killed at Salamis.

head: Ἀρχέδημος
text: Archedemus, an Athenian demagogue with sore eyes, mocked by Aristophanes; in 406 BC he took the first step against the generals of Arginusae.

head: Ἀρχένομος
text: Archenomus, an Athenian whom Pluto summons to Hades at the end of Frogs.

head: Ἀρχεπτόλεμος
text: Archeptolemus, son of Hippodamus, an Athenian who brought Sparta's offer of peace after Pylos, which Cleon had rejected.

head: Ἀσιάδης
text: Asian, of Asia; Ἀσιὰς γῆ or ἤπειρος, the land or continent of Asia.

head: Ἀσιανός
text: Asian, of Asia, including Asia Minor and the lands farther east such as Persia. The plays use the feminine forms Ἀσιᾶτις and Ἀσιῆτις with words for land.

head: Ἀσκληπίδης
text: son of Asclepius (Ἀσκληπιός), the god of healing; οἱ Ἀσκληπιάδαι, his sons, the healers in the Greek camp at Troy.

head: Ἀσκληπιάδαι
text: the Asclepiads, sons and descendants of Asclepius, god of healing: his sons Machaon and Podalirius, doctors with the Greeks at Troy, and the physicians who claimed his line.

head: Ἀσκληπιάδης
text: son or descendant of Asclepius, the god of healing; hence a doctor. The plural Ἀσκληπιάδαι means the guild of physicians.

head: Ἀσκώνδης
text: Ascondas, the wrestler whom the old fighter Ephudion beat in the pancration at Olympia, an exploit Philocleon is told to cite in Wasps.

head: Ἀστάσπης
text: Astaspes, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Ἀσωπίη
text: Ionic form of Ἀσωπία: the land of the Asopus, the river of Boeotia near Thebes; γῆ Ἀσωπία, Boeotian, Theban land.

head: Ἀσωπιάς
text: of Asopus, the river god of Boeotia; Ἀσωπιάδες κόραι, his daughters, the nymphs of the Theban rivers.

head: Ἀσωπός
text: Asopus, a river of Boeotia south of Thebes, and its river god, father of many nymphs. Agamemnon's beacons cross its plain on their way from Troy.

head: Ἀταλάντη
text: Atalanta, the Arcadian huntress, mother of Parthenopaeus, one of the Seven against Thebes.

head: Ἀτρεύς
text: Atreus, son of Pelops, king of Mycenae, and father of Agamemnon and Menelaus. His feud with his brother Thyestes, whose children he served him at a feast, brought the curse on his house.

head: Ἀχαρνεύς
text: Acharnian, a man of Acharnae, the largest deme of Attica, known for its charcoal-burners. The old Acharnians form the chorus of Aristophanes' Acharnians.

head: Ἀχαρνηΐδης
text: men of Acharnae (Ἀχαρναί), the Attic deme; the chorus of Acharnians.

head: Ἀχαρνικός
text: of Acharnae, the largest deme of Attica, north of Athens, known for its charcoal-burners; Acharnian. οἱ Ἀχαρνικοί, the Acharnian old men of the chorus.

head: Ἀχερόντιος
text: of Acheron, the river of the underworld; hence of the dead or of Hades.

head: Ἀχερούσιος
text: of Acheron, the river of the underworld.

head: Ἐξηκεστίδης
text: Execestides, an Athenian mocked in Birds as a Carian, a foreigner passing himself off as a citizen; even he, the joke runs, could not find his homeland from here.

head: Ἐφουδίων
text: Ephudion, an old pancratiast who beat Ascondas at Olympia; the model of the tough old fighter in Wasps.

head: Ἐκβάτανα
text: Ecbatana, the capital of Media and a seat of the Persian kings; in Aristophanes a byword for Persian wealth and splendour.

head: Ἐλευθερίς
text: of Eleutherae, a town on the border of Attica and Boeotia below Cithaeron; there Theseus buries the Argive dead in Suppliant Women.

head: Ἐλύμνιον
text: Elymnium, the place Trygaeus tells the oracle-monger Hierocles, a man of Oreus in Euboea, to fly off to.

head: Ἐπειός
text: Epeius, son of Panopeus, from Phocis, who built the wooden horse with Athena's help. οἱ Ἐπειοί, the Epeans, the old people of Elis.

head: Ἐπίδαυρος
text: Epidaurus, a city on the east coast of Argolis, an enemy of Athens during the war.

head: Ἐπιδαύριος
text: Epidaurian, of Epidaurus in Argolis, a city famous for its shrine of Asclepius.

head: Ἐράσινος
text: Erasinus, a river of the Argolid, near Argos.

head: Ἐρασινίδης
text: Erasinides, an Athenian general at Arginusae in 406 BC, put to death with his colleagues after the battle.

head: Ἐρεχθείδης
text: descendant of Erechtheus, the early king of Athens; hence Athenian. οἱ Ἐρεχθεῖδαι, the Athenians.

head: Ἐρεχθεῖδαι
text: the Erechtheids, descendants of Erechtheus, the early king of Athens; hence the Athenians.

head: Ἐρυμάνθιος
text: Erymanthian, of Erymanthus, the mountain range in northwest Arcadia; the Erymanthian boar was one of the beasts Heracles caught.

head: Ἐρυθεία
text: Erytheia, the island in the far west where Heracles killed the three-bodied herdsman Geryon and took his cattle.

head: Ἐτέοκλος
text: Eteoclus, son of Iphis, an Argive and one of the Seven against Thebes in Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides; not the same man as Eteocles, Oedipus' son.

head: Ἐτεοκλῆς
text: Eteocles, son of Oedipus and Jocasta. He and his brother Polynices were to rule Thebes in turn; he would not give up the throne, and the brothers killed each other when the Seven attacked the city.

head: Ἠδωνίς
text: Edonian, of the Edonians, a Thracian people near the Strymon; Ἠδωνὶς αἶα, Edonian land, Thrace.

head: Ἠδωνός
text: Edonian, of the Edoni, a Thracian people; hence Thracian. Lycurgus, who opposed Dionysus, was their king.

head: Ἠδωνοί
text: the Edonians, a Thracian people near the Strymon; their king Lycurgus, son of Dryas, fought Dionysus and was shut up in rock.

head: Ἠλέκτραι
text: the Electran Gates (Ἠλέκτραι πύλαι), one of the seven gates of Thebes; Capaneus attacks there.

head: Ἠλέκτρη
text: Ionic form of Ἠλέκτρα: Electra, daughter of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, sister of Orestes, Iphigenia, and Chrysothemis. She helps Orestes kill their mother. Also the Electran Gate of Thebes, named after a sister of Cadmus.

head: Ἠλεῖος
text: of Elis, the district of the north-west Peloponnese around Olympia; Elean. In Birds, Lepreus in Elis is offered as a place to live.

head: Ἠλεκτρύων
text: Electryon, son of Perseus, king of Mycenae and father of Alcmene; Amphitryon killed him, and for that was exiled to Thebes.

head: Ἰαόνιος
text: Ionian (an old poetic form): of the Ionians, the Greeks of Asia Minor and the islands. Ἰαόνιοι νόμοι, Ionian strains of lament.

head: Ἰαπετός
text: Iapetus, a Titan, son of Uranus and Gaia and father of Prometheus and Atlas; in Clouds a byword for someone hopelessly old-fashioned.

head: Ἰφιγόνη
text: Iphigone, a short form of Ἰφιγένεια: Iphigenia, the daughter Agamemnon sacrificed at Aulis.

head: Ἰλιόθεν
text: from Ilium (Ἴλιον), that is, from Troy.

head: Ἰλιοφθόρος
text: destroying Ilium (Troy).

head: Ἰμαῖος
text: Imaeus, a Persian archer named among the leaders in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Ἰνάχειος
text: of Inachus (Ἴναχος), the river god and first king of Argos; ἡ Ἰναχεία, Io, his daughter.

head: Ἰναχίδης
text: son or descendant of Inachus (Ἴναχος), the river god and first king of Argos; hence Argive. οἱ Ἰναχίδαι, the Argives.

head: Ἰνδή
text: Indian (fem.); αἱ Ἰνδαί, Indian women, who ride on camels in Aeschylus' Suppliant Women.

head: Ἰόλαος
text: Iolaus, son of Iphicles and nephew of Heracles, his charioteer and companion. In Children of Heracles, old and frail, he protects Heracles' children at Athens and is made young again for the battle.

head: Ἰόλη
text: Iole, daughter of Eurytus, king of Oechalia. Heracles sacks Oechalia to win her and sends her home as a captive, which drives Deianira to send him the poisoned robe in Women of Trachis.

head: Ἰοφῶν
text: Iophon, son of Sophocles and a tragic poet himself. In Frogs, Dionysus calls him the only good tragedian left, but wonders how much his father helped him.

head: Ἰοκάστη
text: Jocasta, daughter of Menoeceus, wife of Laius and mother of Oedipus, whom she later married without knowing him. In Sophocles she hangs herself; in Euripides' Phoenician Women she lives on and dies over her sons.

head: Ἰούλιος
text: Julius, named as the father of an old man mocked in Knights 407. Some texts instead read Οὐλίου, Ulius.

head: Ἰθακήσιος
text: of Ithaca, the island off western Greece, home of Odysseus; Ithacan.

head: Ἰσμήνη
text: Ismene, daughter of Oedipus and Jocasta, sister of Antigone, Eteocles, and Polyneices. In Antigone she refuses to help bury Polyneices, then asks to share her sister's death.

head: Ἰσμήνιος
text: of the Ismenus, the river of Thebes; Ismenian, Theban.

head: Ἰσμήνιχος
text: Ismenichus, a Boeotian slave's name in Acharnians.

head: Ἰσμηνίας
text: Ismenias, a Theban name. In Acharnians the Theban trader's slave is Ismenias; in Lysistrata Ismenia is the Theban girl the women call their friend.

head: Ἰσμηνός
text: Ismenus, a river beside Thebes, near which stood the temple of Ismenian Apollo.

head: Ἰώλκιος
text: of Iolcus, the city in Thessaly at the foot of Pelion, where Pelias ruled and from which Jason sailed.

head: Ἰωλκός
text: Iolcus, a city of Magnesia in Thessaly at the foot of Mount Pelion: home of Pelias, of his daughter Alcestis, and of Jason, and the port from which the Argo sailed.

head: Ὀδόμαντοι
text: the Odomanti, a Thracian tribe. In Acharnians a troop of them, hired as mercenaries, steals Dicaeopolis' garlic.

head: Ὀλοφύξιος
text: of Olophyxus, a small town on the Athos peninsula; in Birds a decree tells Cloudcuckooland to use the same measures 'as the Olophyxians'.

head: Ὀμφάλη
text: Omphale, queen of Lydia. Heracles was sold to her as a slave for a year, as penance for killing Iphitus.

head: Ὀνούποκαι
text: Onoupokai ("Donkey-shearings"), a made-up place in Hades in Frogs.

head: Ὀπούντιοι
text: the Opuntians, the Locrians of Opus on the east coast of Greece.

head: Ὀπούντιος
text: of Opus, the chief town of the eastern Locrians; Opuntian. In Birds also the name of a one-eyed Athenian nicknamed the Raven.

head: Ὀρνέη
text: Orneae, a town in the Argolid; in Birds "to die at Orneae" puns on ὄρνεον, bird.

head: Ὀρθαγόρης
text: Ionic form of Ὀρθαγόρας: Orthagoras ("upright"), a comic name with a sexual sense; in Assemblywomen a young woman tells an old one to call on him for her pleasure.

head: Ὀρσίλοχος
text: Orsilochus, an Athenian who kept a brothel; in Lysistrata a woman tries to fly off to his house.

head: Αἴγισθος
text: Aegisthus, son of Thyestes and cousin of Agamemnon. He becomes Clytemnestra's lover, helps her kill Agamemnon, and rules Argos until Orestes kills him.

head: Αἴσωπος
text: Aesop, the writer of fables, of the sixth century BC; Aristophanes' characters quote his animal stories.

head: Αἴτνη
text: Aetna, the volcano in north-east Sicily; in Cyclops the Cyclopes live on its slopes. In Birds a poet hails Peisthetaerus as founder of Aetna, the city at its foot.

head: Αἰακίδης
text: son or descendant of Aeacus (Αἰακός): Peleus and Telamon, and their sons Achilles and Ajax.

head: Αἰακός
text: Aeacus, son of Zeus and Aegina, king of Aegina, father of Peleus and Telamon and grandfather of Achilles and Ajax. After death a judge in Hades; in Frogs he keeps Pluto's door.

head: Αἰξωνεύς
text: Aexonian, of the Attic deme Aexone, on the coast south of Athens. In Wasps the dog Labes, standing for the general Laches, is from Aexone.

head: Αἰγεΐδης
text: son of Aegeus (Αἰγεύς): Theseus; hence an Athenian.

head: Αἰγεύς
text: Aegeus, king of Athens and father of Theseus. In Medea he passes through Corinth and promises Medea a refuge in Athens.

head: Αἰνιάν
text: Aenianian, of the Aenianes, a people of southern Thessaly in the valley of the Spercheius.

head: Αἰσωπικός
text: Aesopic, of Aesop, the writer of fables.

head: Αἰσχίνης
text: Aeschines, son of Sellus, an Athenian whom Aristophanes mocks as a boaster about wealth he did not have.

head: Αἰσχινάδης
text: Aeschinades, a farmer neighbour in Peace, from whom Trygaeus' household is to fetch myrtle berries.

head: Αἰσχύλος
text: Aeschylus (525–456 BC), the Athenian tragic poet of Eleusis, who fought at Marathon. In Aristophanes' Frogs he contends with Euripides in Hades and wins the right to return to Athens.

head: Αἰτωλίς
text: Aetolian, of Aetolia in western Greece; Αἰτωλὶς γῆ, the land of Aetolia.

head: Αἰτωλός
text: Aetolian, of Aetolia, the region of western Greece north of the Corinthian gulf; Tydeus, son of Oeneus, is the Aetolian among the Seven. οἱ Αἰτωλοί, the Aetolians.

head: Αἰτωλοί
text: the Aetolians, the people of Aetolia in western Greece, known as javelin men. Tydeus, father of Diomedes, came from there.

head: Αὐτομένης
text: Automenes, an Athenian praised in mock terms in Wasps for his three sons: a lyre player, an actor, and the vile Ariphrades.

head: Βάκτριος
text: Bactrian, of Bactria, a far eastern province of the Persian empire.

head: Βαρκαῖος
text: of Barca, a Greek city of Cyrenaica in Libya; in Electra a Barcaean chariot is one of the teams in the race.

head: Βατανώχος
text: Batanochus, a Persian, father of Alpistus, named in the lament of Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Βδελυκλέων
text: Bdelycleon ('Cleon-loather'), the son in Aristophanes' Wasps, who tries to cure his father Philocleon of his passion for jury service.

head: Βελλεροφόντης
text: Bellerophon, grandson of Sisyphus, who rode the winged horse Pegasus and killed the Chimaera. Aristophanes mocks the hero of Euripides' Bellerophon, a lame beggar in rags.

head: Βίστονες
text: the Bistones, a Thracian people near Abdera; Diomedes, whose man-eating horses Heracles must fetch, is their king.

head: Βλέπυρος
text: Blepyrus, Praxagora's husband in Aristophanes' Assemblywomen, who goes out in her clothes because she has taken his.

head: Βλεψίδημος
text: Blepsidemus, Chremylus' friend in Aristophanes' Wealth, who suspects that Chremylus' sudden riches must be stolen.

head: Βοίβιος
text: of Boebe, the lake and town in Thessaly near Pherae, where Admetus has his home.

head: Βοιώτιος
text: Boeotian, of Boeotia, the region north of Attica whose chief city is Thebes. In Acharnians a Boeotian brings his goods to Dicaeopolis' private market.

head: Βοιωτία
text: Boeotia, the region of central Greece north of Attica; its chief city is Thebes.

head: Βορραῖος
text: of Boreas, the north wind; northern. In Seven against Thebes, the Northern Gate.

head: Βούπαλος
text: Bupalus, a sculptor of Chios who made a mocking likeness of the poet Hipponax, who answered with savage verse.

head: Βρασίδης
text: Ionic form of Βρασίδας: Brasidas, the leading Spartan general of the early Peloponnesian War, killed at Amphipolis in 422 BC.

head: Βραυρώνιος
text: of Brauron, the Attic deme with the shrine of Artemis Brauronia. In Iphigenia in Tauris Iphigenia is to serve her there; in Lysistrata girls served there as "bears".

head: Βραυρῶνάδε
text: to Brauron, the Attic deme on the east coast with a sanctuary of Artemis, where Athenians went for her festival.

head: Βυζάντιος
text: of Byzantium, the Greek city on the Bosporus.

head: Ξάνθιππος
text: Xanthippus, a name with "horse" in it that Strepsiades' wife wanted for their son in Clouds.

head: Ξανθίδιον
text: little Xanthias, a pet form of Xanthias, Dionysus' slave in Frogs.

head: Ξένυλλα
text: Xenylla, an Athenian woman in a comic tale of women's doings in Thesmophoriazusae.

head: Ξέρξης
text: Xerxes, son of Darius and Atossa, king of Persia 486–465 BC. He led the invasion of Greece that failed at Salamis in 480, and comes home in ruin in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Ξενόφαντος
text: Xenophantus, father of Hieronymus, a shaggy-haired dithyrambic poet; Clouds mocks 'the son of Xenophantus'.

head: Ξενοκλέης
text: Ionic form of Ξενοκλῆς: Xenocles, an Athenian tragic poet, son of Carcinus, mocked by Aristophanes as a bad poet.

head: Δάτις
text: Datis, the Mede who commanded with Artaphernes the Persian force beaten at Marathon in 490 BC. In Peace Trygaeus sings 'the song of Datis', a line of broken Greek.

head: Δαδάκης
text: Dadaces, a Persian commander of a thousand, killed at Salamis in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Δαναίδαι
text: Danaids, sons of Danaus; in Euripides a name for the Greeks at Troy, like Danaans (Δαναοί).

head: Δαναίδες
text: Danaids, the fifty daughters of Danaus, all but Hypermnestra of whom killed their bridegrooms on their wedding night; Antigone threatens to be one of them. In Iphigenia at Aulis the cited forms belong to Δαναΐδαι, the Danaans, the Greek army.

head: Δαναός
text: Danaus, son of Belus and twin of Aegyptus. He fled from Egypt to Argos with his fifty daughters to escape their marriage to Aegyptus' fifty sons, and became king there; the Greeks were called Danaans after him.

head: Δαρδάνειος
text: of Dardanus, ancestor of the Trojan kings; Dardanian, Trojan. τὰ Δαρδάνεια μέλαθρα, the halls of Troy.

head: Δαρδάνιος
text: of Dardanus, the ancestor of the Trojan kings; hence Trojan.

head: Δαρδανία
text: Dardania, the land of Dardanus around Troy; in the plays simply Troy.

head: Δαρδανίδης
text: son or descendant of Dardanus, ancestor of the Trojan kings; a Trojan. In Iphigenia at Aulis ὁ Δαρδανίδας is Ganymede; in the plural, the Trojans.

head: Δαρδανίς
text: of Dardanus, the founder of the Trojan royal line; hence Trojan. οἱ Δαρδανίδαι, the Trojans. In Wasps Dardanis is the flute girl Philocleon brings home.

head: Δαύλιος
text: Daulian, of Daulis, a town of Phocis; the disguised Orestes calls himself a Daulian.

head: Δαυλία
text: Daulia or Daulis, a town of Phocis, near the place where the roads from Delphi and Daulia meet, where Oedipus killed Laius.

head: Δαυλιεύς
text: Daulian, of Daulis in Phocis.

head: Δεξίνικος
text: Dexinicus, a spectator in Wealth who jumps up to catch the figs and sweets thrown to the audience.

head: Δεξίθεος
text: Dexitheus, a lyre-singer at Athens whose Boeotian song pleased Dicaeopolis in Acharnians.

head: Δελφικός
text: of Delphi, the seat of Apollo's oracle below Mount Parnassus in Phocis; Delphic.

head: Δερκέτης
text: Dercetes of Phyle, the farmer in Acharnians who has lost his oxen and begs Dicaeopolis for some of his peace.

head: Δερκύλος
text: Dercylus, a name in the opening of Wasps, one of the audience the slaves pretend to hear guessing at their master's sickness.

head: Δηλιάς
text: Delian, of Delos, the island where Leto bore Apollo and Artemis; αἱ Δηλιάδες, the Delian maidens who sing and dance for Apollo.

head: Δημητρίη
text: Ionic form of Δημητρία: Demetria, a woman's name, one of the feminine names Strepsiades lists in Clouds.

head: Δημόστρατος
text: Demostratus, the Athenian orator who proposed the Sicilian expedition of 415 BC; in Lysistrata his wife wails for Adonis while he speaks.

head: Δημολογοκλέων
text: Demologocleon ("people-talk-Cleon"), the comic name the chorus of Wasps gives to Bdelycleon.

head: Δίαιξις
text: Diaixis, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Δίρφυς
text: Dirphys, a mountain in Euboea.

head: Δίρκη
text: Dirce, wife of Lycus of Thebes, killed by Amphion and Zethus for her cruelty to their mother Antiope; also the spring at Thebes named after her, which the poets use for Thebes itself.

head: Διαγόρης
text: Diagoras of Melos, a poet held throughout antiquity to be an atheist; Athens put a price on his head.

head: Διειπετής
text: fallen from Zeus, from the sky; of water, clear, bright. In Bacchae, of the sky: clearer than before.

head: Διειτρέφης
text: Diitrephes, an Athenian who made wicker flasks and rose to command the cavalry; in 413 BC he led the Thracians who sacked Mycalessus.

head: Διόμεια
text: the Diomeia, an Attic deme near Athens named after Diomus, a companion of Heracles; a festival of Heracles was held there.

head: Διοκλέης
text: Ionic form of Διοκλῆς: Diocles, an Athenian exile who died at Megara shielding a youth in battle; the Megarians held games for him, and the Megarian in Acharnians swears by him.

head: Διομήδειος
text: Diomedean. "A Diomedean necessity" was a proverb for a hard compulsion.

head: Διοπείθης
text: Diopeithes, an Athenian dealer in oracles in Aristophanes' day, mocked by the comic poets as half madman, half fraud.

head: Διοσκόρος
text: Dioscurus ("son of Zeus"); in the plural the Dioscuri, Castor and Polydeuces, brothers of Helen and Clytemnestra, later gods who save sailors.

head: Διρκαῖος
text: of Dirce, the spring at Thebes; hence Theban.

head: Διτύλης
text: Ditylas, a slave whom Aeacus calls out in Frogs to tie up Xanthias.

head: Δοτάμας
text: Dotamas, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, mourned among the dead.

head: Δρακοντίδης
text: Dracontides, an Athenian often tried in the courts, whom Philocleon in Wasps fears will get off. At Wasps 438 Cecrops, a snake below the waist, is hailed as 'Dracontides below the feet', a pun.

head: Δῶρος
text: Dorus, ancestor of the Dorians. In Ion Athena foretells that Creusa will bear him to Xuthus.

head: Δωδωναῖος
text: of Dodona, the town in Epirus with the oldest oracle of Zeus in Greece; Dodonaean.

head: Εὔδαμος
text: Eudamus, an Athenian of Aristophanes' day who sold rings as charms against poison.

head: Εὔηνος
text: Evenus, the river of Aetolia where the Centaur Nessus carried travellers across for pay and laid hands on Deianeira.

head: Εὐάδνη
text: Evadne, daughter of Iphis and wife of Capaneus, who throws herself on her husband's pyre in Euripides' Suppliant Women.

head: Εὐβοΐς
text: Euboean, of Euboea (feminine).

head: Εὐβοίς
text: Euboean (fem.), of Euboea, the long island off the coast of Attica and Boeotia.

head: Εὐβοικός
text: Euboean, of Euboea, the long island off the east coast of Boeotia and Attica.

head: Εὐβούλη
text: Eubule ('good counsel'), a woman's name in Thesmophoriazusae: the chorus says Eubule is better than any of last year's councillors.

head: Εὐελπίδης
text: Euelpides ("good hope"), one of the two Athenians who leave the city in Birds and found the city of birds with Peisetaerus.

head: Εὐεργίδης
text: Euergides, one of the old jurors of Wasps.

head: Εὐφήμιος
text: Euphemius, an Athenian named in Wasps as an equal of Theorus, a flatterer of Cleon; nothing else is known of him.

head: Εὐφορίδης
text: Euphorides, a poor, hard-working Acharnian, named as one who never served on a paid embassy.

head: Εὐκράτης
text: Eucrates. 1. An Athenian demagogue, a seller of tow, who led the people before Cleon (Knights). 2. In Lysistrata, a general guarding Thrace, likely the brother of Nicias.

head: Εὐμολπίδαι
text: the Eumolpidae, the priestly family of Eleusis, descendants of Eumolpus, who led the Mysteries.

head: Εὐθυμένης
text: Euthymenes, archon at Athens in 437/6 BC, the year the envoys in Acharnians set out for Persia.

head: Εὐρύτιος
text: of Eurytus, king of Oechalia; in Hippolytus, the house of Eurytus, from which Heracles took Iole.

head: Εὐρυδίκη
text: Eurydice, wife of Creon, king of Thebes, in Sophocles' Antigone; she kills herself on hearing that her son Haemon is dead.

head: Εὐρυκλέης
text: Ionic form of Εὐρυκλῆς: Eurycles, a famous Athenian ventriloquist prophet. Aristophanes says that like him he spoke from inside other men's bellies, writing for other poets.

head: Εὐρυσθεύς
text: Eurystheus, son of Sthenelus, king of Argos (Tiryns and Mycenae), who set Heracles his labours. In Children of Heracles he hunts Heracles' children and is taken prisoner by the Athenians.

head: Εὐρυτεῖος
text: of Eurytus (Εὔρυτος), king of Oechalia; Eurytus' city, which Heracles sacked to take his daughter Iole.

head: Εὐρώτης
text: Ionic form of Εὐρώτας: Eurotas, the river of Laconia that flows past Sparta; the plays use it for Sparta and Helen's home.

head: Εὐχαρίδης
text: Eucharides, an Athenian shopkeeper in Wasps from whom Philocleon sends for three heads of garlic.

head: Φάρσαλος
text: Pharsalus, a city of Thessaly; Euripides makes it the home of Peleus and Achilles. In Wasps an Athenian goes there on an embassy.

head: Φάϋλλος
text: Phayllus of Croton, the famous athlete and runner who fought for the Greeks at Salamis; the old men of Acharnians and Philocleon in Wasps boast of their youth beside him.

head: Φαιδρίης
text: Ionic form of Φαιδρίας: Phaedrias, one of the old men of the chorus in Lysistrata.

head: Φαιναρέτη
text: Phaenarete, grandmother of Amphitheus in his mock family tree in Acharnians.

head: Φαληρικός
text: of Phalerum, the old harbour of Athens on the bay east of Piraeus. ἀφύαι Φαληρικαί, Phaleric small fry, a prized fish dish.

head: Φανοτεύς
text: Phanoteus, a Phocian, ally of Clytemnestra and Aegisthus. In Electra the old tutor claims to come from him with the false news of Orestes' death.

head: Φαρανδάκης
text: Pharandaces, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, named in the muster and mourned among the dead.

head: Φαρνάκης
text: Pharnaces, Persian satrap of the lands near the Hellespont; in Birds the Athenian inspector lets slip that he has dealings with him.

head: Φαρνοῦχος
text: Pharnuchus, a Persian commander killed at Salamis in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Φαρσάλιος
text: of Pharsalus, a city of Thessaly near Phthia, where Andromache lives in Euripides' play.

head: Φασιανικός
text: Phasian, of the Phasis, the river of Colchis; ὄρνις Φασιανικός, the pheasant. One of the Athenian visitors in Birds calls himself a Phasian bird, with a joke about informing.

head: Φειδίης
text: Ionic form of Φειδίας: Phidias, the greatest Athenian sculptor, friend of Pericles. In Peace Hermes says his disgrace began the war.

head: Φειδιππίδης
text: Pheidippides, the horse-mad son of Strepsiades in Aristophanes' Clouds, whose debts drive his father to Socrates' school.

head: Φειδιππίδιον
text: little Pheidippides, the father's pet form of Φειδιππίδης in Clouds.

head: Φερέδειπνος
text: Pheredeipnus ("dinner-bringer"), an old juror whom Philocleon calls to his help in Wasps.

head: Φερεκράτης
text: Pherecrates, an Athenian poet of Old Comedy, older than Aristophanes; Lysistrata quotes his saying about flaying a flayed dog.

head: Φερητιάδης
text: son or grandson of Pheres: Eumelus, son of Admetus, the charioteer in Iphigenia at Aulis.

head: Φίλιννα
text: Philinna, a common Greek woman's name; in Clouds Strepsiades lists it among names that are plainly female.

head: Φιλάμμων
text: Philammon, a mythical singer, son of Apollo, father of the Thracian bard Thamyris.

head: Φιλαινέτη
text: Philaenete, one of the women gathering for the assembly in Ecclesiazusae.

head: Φιλόστρατος
text: Philostratus, an Athenian brothel-keeper mocked by Aristophanes as 'the dog-fox'.

head: Φιλοδώρητος
text: Philodoretus, an Athenian named in Assemblywomen as the husband of one of the women.

head: Φιλοκλέης
text: Ionic form of Φιλοκλῆς: Philocles, an Athenian tragic poet, nephew of Aeschylus, mocked by Aristophanes as ugly and harsh in his verse.

head: Φιλοκλέων
text: Philocleon ("Cleon-lover"), the old man in Aristophanes' Wasps who is mad for jury service, whom his son Bdelycleon tries to cure.

head: Φιλοκράτης
text: Philocrates, the bird-seller in Birds who sold the two Athenians their jackdaw and crow; the birds put a price on his head.

head: Φιλοκτήτης
text: Philoctetes, son of Poeas, the great archer who holds the bow of Heracles. The Greeks left him on Lemnos with a festering snakebite; in Sophocles' play they must bring him to Troy.

head: Φιλοῦργος
text: Philurgus, one of the old men of the chorus in Lysistrata.

head: Φιλωνίδης
text: Philonides of Melite, a rich Athenian of Aristophanes' day, mocked as gross and stupid; the courtesan Lais was his mistress.

head: Φινείδης
text: son of Phineus (Φινεύς), the Thracian king; in Antigone his two sons, blinded by their stepmother.

head: Φινεύς
text: Phineus, king of Salmydessus in Thrace, a blind prophet whose meals the Harpies snatched.

head: Φινηΐς
text: of Phineus (Φινεύς), the blind seer-king of Salmydessus in Thrace; the shore of Phineus, on the Black Sea route.

head: Φλέγρη
text: Phlegra, the place in the north where the gods fought and beat the Giants; later identified with Pallene in Chalcidice.

head: Φλεγραῖος
text: Phlegraean, of Phlegra, the plain where the gods fought and beat the Giants, placed on the peninsula of Pallene in Chalcidice.

head: Φλυεύς
text: of the Attic deme Phlya; Chabes of Phlya is one of the old jurors in Wasps.

head: Φολόη
text: Pholoe, the mountain in Elis where the Centaurs lived; Heracles fought them there.

head: Φορμίσιος
text: Phormisius, an Athenian politician of the late fifth century BC, mocked for his shaggy hair. In Frogs Euripides names him as a pupil of Aeschylus.

head: Φθιῶτις
text: Phthiotis or Phthia, the region of southern Thessaly ruled by Peleus; the home of Achilles and his son Neoptolemus. As an adjective, of Phthia.

head: Φρύνιχος
text: Phrynichus, an early Athenian tragic poet, at work from about 510 to 476 BC, praised in Birds and Frogs for the sweetness of his songs. Aristophanes also names a comic poet, a dancing actor, and an oligarch general so called.

head: Φρῦνις
text: Phrynis, a lyre-singer of Mytilene at Athens in the Peloponnesian War, known for new-fangled music.

head: Φρυνώνδης
text: Phrynondas, an Athenian whose name became a byword for a rogue.

head: Φυλεύς
text: Phyleus, son of Augeas and father of Meges; he sided with Heracles against his father and moved to Dulichium.

head: Φυρόμαχος
text: Phyromachus, an Athenian speaker remembered in Ecclesiazusae for a slip of the tongue that made a sexual joke.

head: Φῶκος
text: Phocus, son of Aeacus by the Nereid Psamathe, half-brother of Peleus and Telamon, who killed him; in Andromache Menelaus throws the murder in Peleus' face.

head: Γανυμήδης
text: Ganymede, son of Tros, the most beautiful of mortals, whom the gods carried off from Troy to be Zeus' cupbearer and darling.

head: Γαργηττόθεν
text: from Gargettus, a deme of Attica north-east of Athens.

head: Γέρης
text: Geres, an old man in Assemblywomen, the only lover the young woman says the old woman can get.

head: Γερητοθεόδωρος
text: Geres-Theodoruses, a joke compound of two names in Acharnians, for Athenians who draw pay on embassies far away.

head: Γευσιστράτη
text: Geusistrate, a tavern-keeper's wife among the women in Aristophanes' Assemblywomen.

head: Γλαυκέτης
text: Glauketes, an Athenian glutton mocked by Aristophanes; in Thesmophoriazusae he stands in for the sea monster that will eat the bound captive.

head: Γόργασος
text: Gorgasus, father of the Athenian general Lamachus, named in Acharnians.

head: Γοργίης
text: Ionic form of Γοργίας: Gorgias of Leontini in Sicily, the famous teacher of rhetoric. Aristophanes mocks him and his pupils.

head: Γουνεύς
text: Guneus, leader of the Aenianes in the fleet at Aulis.

head: Γρύττος
text: Gryttus, an Athenian, a notorious male prostitute; in Knights Paphlagon boasts that he put a stop to such men by striking out Gryttus.

head: Καδμεῖος
text: of Cadmus, the founder of Thebes; hence Theban. οἱ Καδμεῖοι, the Thebans.

head: Καφήρειος
text: of Caphareus, the rocky south-east cape of Euboea, where the Greek fleet was wrecked on the way home from Troy.

head: Καφηρίς
text: of Caphareus, the rocky cape at the southeast tip of Euboea, where Nauplius lit false fires and wrecked the Greek fleet sailing home from Troy.

head: Καλλιππίδης
text: Callippides, one of the horsey names Strepsiades' wife wants for their son in Clouds.

head: Καμάρινα
text: Camarina, a Greek city on the south coast of Sicily.

head: Καννωνός
text: Cannonus, author of a decree that an accused man must plead held on both sides; in Assemblywomen the young man pulled by two hags jokes on it.

head: Καπανεύς
text: Capaneus, son of Hipponous, one of the Seven against Thebes. He boasted that not even Zeus could stop him scaling the walls, and Zeus struck him down with a thunderbolt. His wife Evadne leapt onto his pyre.

head: Καρδοπίων
text: Cardopion, a figure in a fable Philocleon begins to tell in Wasps ("how Cardopion and his mother…"); the story is lost.

head: Καρκινίτης
text: son of Carcinus (Καρκίνος), the tragic poet. In Wasps his small sons dance; the name also puns on καρκίνος, crab.

head: Καρύστιος
text: Carystian, of Carystus, a town on the south coast of Euboea; οἱ Καρύστιοι, the Carystians, guests at the feast in Lysistrata.

head: Κασάνδρη
text: Ionic form of Κασσάνδρα: Cassandra, daughter of Priam and Hecuba, a prophet whom no one believed. Agamemnon brings her home as his prize, and Clytemnestra kills her with him.

head: Κασσάνδρη
text: Ionic form of Κασσάνδρα: Cassandra, daughter of Priam and Hecuba, a prophetess whom no one believes. Agamemnon brings her home from Troy as his prize, and Clytemnestra kills her with him.

head: Κεβριόνης
text: Cebriones, one of the Giants who fought the gods; in Birds he and Porphyrion are hailed at the sight of the birds' city.

head: Κερχνεία
text: Cerchneia, a spring near Lerna in the Argolid, to which Io runs in Prometheus Bound.

head: Κήναιον
text: Cenaeum, the north-west cape of Euboea, with an altar of Zeus Cenaeus where Heracles sacrifices in Trachiniae.

head: Κηφισόδημος
text: Cephisodemus, named in Acharnians as the father of the young speaker whom the chorus attacks for prosecuting the aged Thucydides.

head: Κηφισοφῶν
text: Cephisophon, a friend of Euripides, said to have acted in his plays and helped him write them. In Frogs Aeschylus mocks Euripides for his help.

head: Κηκείδης
text: Ceceides, an old dithyrambic poet; in Clouds Wrong Logic names him as old-fashioned.

head: Κηναῖος
text: Cenaean, of Cenaeum, the cape at the northwest tip of Euboea; Ζεὺς Κηναῖος, Zeus of Cenaeum, at whose altar Heracles puts on the poisoned robe.

head: Κίμων
text: Cimon, son of Miltiades, the Athenian general who led 4,000 hoplites to save Sparta during the helot revolt.

head: Κικυννεύς
text: of Cicynna, an Attic deme; the deme of Strepsiades in Clouds.

head: Κιλλικῶν
text: Cillicon, a traitor of proverb who betrayed his city and, asked what he was doing, said "nothing bad".

head: Κιμβερικός
text: Cimberic, the name of a fine, sheer dress the women plan to wear in Lysistrata.

head: Κιμμερικός
text: Cimmerian, of the Cimmerian Bosporus, the strait (now of Kerch) that joins the Maeotic lake to the Black Sea. Prometheus tells Io to cross it into Asia.

head: Κιμώλιος
text: of Cimolus, a small island of the Cyclades near Melos; Κιμωλία γῆ, Cimolian earth, a white clay used as soap.

head: Κιμωλία
text: of Cimolus, an island of the Cyclades; Κιμωλία γῆ, Cimolian earth, a white clay used as soap, as in the Frogs' jibe at the bathman Cleigenes.

head: Κινησίης
text: Ionic form of Κινησίας: Cinesias, son of Meles, an Athenian dithyrambic poet mocked by Aristophanes for his thin body and airy verse. In Lysistrata the name goes to Myrrhine's eager husband.

head: Κιθαιρών
text: Cithaeron, the mountain range between Boeotia and Attica, south of Thebes. The infant Oedipus was left to die there, and there the Theban women hold their Bacchic rites and tear Pentheus apart.

head: Κιθαιρώνειος
text: of Cithaeron, the mountain between Boeotia and Attica, where the Bacchic women tear Pentheus apart.

head: Κιθαιρώνιος
text: of Cithaeron, the mountain range between Boeotia and Attica, haunt of Dionysus and his maenads.

head: Κισθήνη
text: Cisthene, a far place at the edge of the world where the Gorgons and the daughters of Phorcys live, in Prometheus Bound.

head: Κλεαίνετος
text: Cleaenetus, an Athenian named in Knights as the author of a decree that took away the generals' free meals in the town hall; perhaps Cleon's father.

head: Κλειδημίδης
text: Cleidemides, an Athenian named in Frogs as the source of news about Sophocles in Hades.

head: Κλειγένης
text: Cleigenes, an Athenian bath-man and meddler in politics, mocked in Frogs as puny, dishonest, and drunken.

head: Κλειναρέτη
text: Cleinarete, one of the women who gather at dawn with Praxagora in Assemblywomen.

head: Κλεινίης
text: Ionic form of Κλεινίας: Clinias; ὁ Κλεινίου, the son of Clinias, is Alcibiades, mocked in Acharnians as a loose-living, glib young speaker.

head: Κλεισθένης
text: Cleisthenes, an Athenian of Aristophanes' day, mocked again and again for his smooth, beardless face and womanish ways; in Thesmophoriazusae he comes to warn the women of the spy.

head: Κλειταγόρη
text: Cleitagora, the heroine of a drinking song sung at Athenian parties, which Aristophanes quotes. Strepsiades also gives it as a woman's name in Clouds.

head: Κλειτοφῶν
text: Cleitophon, an Athenian politician of the late fifth century BC, named in Frogs with Theramenes as a pupil of Euripides.

head: Κλεόκριτος
text: Cleocritus, an Athenian mocked by Aristophanes; Birds calls the ostrich his mother, which suggests he was big and clumsy.

head: Κλεοφῶν
text: Cleophon, an Athenian demagogue at the end of the Peloponnesian War who opposed peace with Sparta; Aristophanes mocks him as a Thracian.

head: Κλεονίκη
text: Cleonice, Lysistrata's neighbour and friend in Aristophanes' Lysistrata; some editions call her Calonice.

head: Κλεώνυμος
text: Cleonymus, an Athenian politician of the 420s BC, mocked by Aristophanes as a glutton and a coward who threw away his shield.

head: Κλεωνύμης
text: Cleonyme, a mock feminine of Cleonymus in Clouds, where Socrates' lesson on genders makes the cowardly Cleonymus a woman.

head: Κλυταιμνήστρα
text: Clytemnestra, daughter of Tyndareus and Leda, sister of Helen, and wife of Agamemnon. With her lover Aegisthus she kills Agamemnon on his return from Troy; her son Orestes kills her in revenge.

head: Κλυταιμνήστρη
text: Ionic form of Κλυταιμνήστρα: Clytemnestra, daughter of Tyndareus and Leda and wife of Agamemnon. With Aegisthus she killed him on his return from Troy; her son Orestes killed her.

head: Κνώσιος
text: Cnossian, of Cnossus, the royal city of Minos in Crete; hence Cretan. ὁ ταῦρος Κνώσιος, the bull of Cnossus, the Minotaur, which Theseus killed.

head: Κοισύρη
text: Ionic form of Κοισύρα: Coesyra, a rich, haughty lady of the Alcmeonid family; her name stood for luxury and airs. ὁ Κοισύρας, 'Coesyra's son', mocks a man of that line.

head: Κονθυλεύς
text: of Conthyle, a deme of Attica; Strymodorus, one of the jurors of Wasps, is from there.

head: Κοθώκιδαι
text: Cothocidae, an Attic deme.

head: Κορκυραῖος
text: Corcyraean, of Corcyra (Corfu); Κορκυραῖα πτερά, 'Corcyraean wings', a joke on the whips made in Corcyra.

head: Κράτινος
text: Cratinus, the great Athenian poet of Old Comedy and Aristophanes' older rival, mocked by him as a drunkard past his prime.

head: Κρᾶθις
text: Crathis, a large river of Bruttium in southern Italy.

head: Κραναΐδης
text: descendant of Cranaus (Κραναός), the early king of Attica; hence Athenian.

head: Κρατῖνος
text: Cratinus, the great Athenian poet of Old Comedy and Aristophanes' elder rival, mocked by him as an old drunkard.

head: Κρεοντεῖος
text: of Creon, Creon's: θρόνοι Κρεόντειοι, Creon's throne, as Oedipus says in his quarrel with Teiresias.

head: Κρεούσα
text: Creusa, daughter of Erechtheus, king of Athens, and wife of Xuthus. Apollo took her by force, and she left their son Ion to die; in Euripides' Ion she finds him again at Delphi.

head: Κρίτυλλα
text: Critylla, an Athenian woman's name. In Thesmophoriazusae the woman guarding Euripides' kinsman, daughter of Antitheus of Gargettus; in Lysistrata a woman the chorus hurries to save.

head: Κριῶθεν
text: from Crioa, a deme of Attica; Euelpides of Birds is from there.

head: Κτησιφῶν
text: Ctesiphon, a fat Athenian; the prize for the drinking match in Acharnians is a wineskin, 'Ctesiphon's belly'.

head: Κύβελα
text: Cybele (Κυβέλη), the great mother goddess of Phrygia, worshipped with drums and wild dancing; the Bacchae joins her rites to those of Dionysus.

head: Κύννα
text: Cynna, an Athenian courtesan, named by Aristophanes beside Cleon and Lysicles.

head: Κυδαθηναιεύς
text: of Cydathenaeum, the Athenian deme of Cleon. In Wasps the dog who brings the charge is "Dog of Cydathenaeum", that is, Cleon.

head: Κυχρεῖος
text: of Cychreus, the old king of Salamis; hence of Salamis.

head: Κυζικηνικός
text: of Cyzicus, the Greek city on the Sea of Marmara. In Peace a cowardly officer dyes himself a Cyzicene colour as he runs away.

head: Κωμαρχίδης
text: Comarchides, a farmer neighbour in Peace, hailed in the chorus's picture of country life after the war.

head: Κωμίης
text: Ionic form of Κωμίας: Comias, one of the old jurors in Wasps.

head: Λάβδακος
text: Labdacus, king of Thebes, son of Polydorus and grandson of Cadmus; father of Laius and grandfather of Oedipus.

head: Λᾶσος
text: Lasus of Hermione, a lyric poet of the late 500s BC who founded the Athenian school of dithyramb and taught Pindar; Wasps tells of his rivalry with Simonides.

head: Λαβδακεῖος
text: of Labdacus, king of Thebes, father of Laius and grandfather of Oedipus.

head: Λαβδακίδαι
text: the Labdacids, the descendants of Labdacus, king of Thebes: his son Laius, Oedipus, and Oedipus' children, a house famous for its misfortunes.

head: Λαβδακίδης
text: son or descendant of Labdacus (Λάβδακος), the Theban king; οἱ Λαβδακίδαι, Laius, Oedipus, and his children.

head: Λαερτιάδης
text: son of Laertes (Λαέρτης): Odysseus.

head: Λαισποδίας
text: Laespodias, an Athenian general of 414 BC; in Birds a god hides his ugly legs under his cloak like him.

head: Λακεδαιμόνιος
text: Lacedaemonian, of Lacedaemon, that is, Sparta; οἱ Λακεδαιμόνιοι, the Spartans, Athens' enemies in the Peloponnesian War.

head: Λακρατείδης
text: Lacrateides, one of the old charcoal-burners of the chorus of Acharnians.

head: Λαμπιτώ
text: Lampito, the Spartan woman in Aristophanes' Lysistrata who joins the strike and brings the women of Sparta into the oath.

head: Λαομεδόντιος
text: of Laomedon, king of Troy and father of Priam; Λαομεδόντιε παῖ, 'son of Laomedon', is Ganymede in Trojan Women.

head: Λαπίθαι
text: the Lapiths, a people of Thessaly who fought the Centaurs at the wedding of their king Pirithous; Peleus fought with them.

head: Λαπίθης
text: a Lapith; οἱ Λαπίθαι, the Lapiths of Thessaly, ruled by Peirithous, who fought the Centaurs at his wedding.

head: Λασθένης
text: Lasthenes, a Theban whom Eteocles sets against Amphiaraus at one of the gates in Seven against Thebes.

head: Λαυρειωτικός
text: of Laurium, the silver-mining district of Attica. "Laurian owls" are Athenian silver coins, which bore an owl.

head: Λέσβιος
text: Lesbian, of Lesbos, the large island off the coast of Asia Minor. The women of Lesbos had a name for oral sex, and κατὰ τοὺς Λεσβίους in Assemblywomen points to it.

head: Λειψύδριον
text: Leipsydrium, a stronghold in the hills of Attica; the old men of Lysistrata recall marching there in their youth against the tyrants.

head: Λευκολόφης
text: Leucolophus (Leucolophides), an Athenian, father of Adeimantus, one of the generals with Alcibiades in 407 BC, whom Pluto in Frogs wants sent down to Hades.

head: Λεώγορος
text: Leogorus, a rich Athenian whom Aristophanes mocks as a glutton.

head: Λεωγόρης
text: Ionic form of Λεωγόρας: Leogoras, a rich Athenian, father of the orator Andocides, mocked by Aristophanes as a gourmet who kept pheasants.

head: Λεωνίδης
text: Leonidas, king of Sparta, who died holding Thermopylae against the Persians in 480 BC; the Spartan song in Lysistrata recalls him.

head: Λεωτροφίδης
text: Leotrophides, an Athenian dithyrambic poet, mocked by the comic poets for his thin body and thin verse.

head: Λήϊτος
text: Leitus, a leader of the Boeotians at Troy, one of the Argonauts.

head: Λήμνιος
text: of Lemnos, the island in the northern Aegean; Lemnian. The Lemnian women murdered their husbands, so 'the Lemnian evil' in Libation Bearers is the byword for crime.

head: Λητῷος
text: of Leto, mother of Apollo and Artemis. Λητῴα κόρη, Artemis.

head: Λίλαιος
text: Lilaeus, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, killed at Salamis.

head: Λίχης
text: Ionic form of Λίχας: Lichas, the herald of Heracles. In Trachiniae he brings Iole to Deianeira and carries the poisoned robe to Heracles, who hurls him into the sea.

head: Λιβυκός
text: Libyan, of Libya, the old name for Africa west of Egypt.

head: Λιγυστίς
text: Ligurian, of the Ligurians of northwest Italy; Euripides gives Circe a Ligurian home.

head: Λικύμνιος
text: of Licymnius, half-brother of Alcmene; in Birds 'Licymnian bolts' parodies Euripides' lost play Licymnius.

head: Λοκρίς
text: Locris, the land of the Locrians in central Greece.

head: Λοκρός
text: Locrian, of Locris in central Greece; οἱ Λοκροί, the Locrians, whom Ajax son of Oileus led to Troy. The Opuntian Locrians lived at Opus.

head: Λύκις
text: Lycis, an Athenian comic poet named in Frogs as a writer of stale jokes.

head: Λύσιλλα
text: Lysilla, a woman's name in Aristophanes: an example of a feminine name in Clouds, and the secretary of the women's assembly in Thesmophoriazusae.

head: Λυκαβηττός
text: Lycabettus, the steep hill northeast of Athens; in Frogs a byword for huge, high-flown words.

head: Λυκῖνος
text: Lycinus, son of Celeus and Phaenarete and father of Amphitheus in his comic family tree in Acharnians.

head: Λυκομήδης
text: Lycomedes, king of Scyros, father of Deidameia and grandfather of Neoptolemus, who was raised in his house.

head: Λυκοῦργος
text: Lycurgus, an Athenian of Aristophanes' day nicknamed "the Ibis" in Birds.

head: Λυθίμνας
text: Lythimnas, a Persian named in the lament of Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Λυρναῖος
text: of Lyrnae or Lyrnessus; in Persians the commander Tharybis is 'Lyrnaean by birth'.

head: Λυσίστρατος
text: Lysistratus, an Athenian of the deme Cholargus, a poor joker and idler of the market place, mocked several times by Aristophanes.

head: Λυσικλέης
text: Ionic form of Λυσικλῆς: Lysicles the sheep dealer, an Athenian demagogue before Cleon, named in Knights in bad company.

head: Λυσικλής
text: Lysicles, the Athenian sheep-dealer and politician who married Aspasia after Pericles died; Aristophanes names him among bad leaders.

head: Λυσικράτης
text: Lysicrates, an Athenian mocked by Aristophanes as a general who took bribes and as an ugly man with a snub nose.

head: Λυσιστράτη
text: Lysistrata ("she who disbands armies"), the Athenian woman who leads the women's strike to end the war in Aristophanes' Lysistrata.

head: Μάραφις
text: Maraphis, a Persian king in the list of Xerxes' forebears in Aeschylus' Persians; editors often bracket the line.

head: Μάρδος
text: Mardus, in Darius' list of kings in Persians, the fifth ruler, a shame to his country, killed by Artaphrenes by a trick.

head: Μάρδων
text: Mardon, a Persian commander of ten thousand in Xerxes' army, named in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Μάταλλος
text: Matallus of Chrysa, a Persian commander of ten thousand men, named among the dead at Salamis in Aeschylus’ Persians.

head: Μαιώτης
text: Maeotian, of Lake Maeotis (the Sea of Azov) north-east of the Black Sea, where the plays put the Amazons and Scythians.

head: Μαλέη
text: Ionic form of Μαλέα: Malea, the cape at the south-east tip of the Peloponnese, where the winds drive ships off course.

head: Μανόδωρος
text: Manodorus, a slave of Peisetaerus in Birds.

head: Μαριανδυνός
text: Mariandynian, of the Mariandyni, a people of Bithynia on the Black Sea, known for their dirges.

head: Μαρικᾶς
text: Maricas, Eupolis' comedy against Hyperbolus, which Clouds accuses of copying Aristophanes' Knights.

head: Μαριλάδης
text: Mariladas, a poor old Acharnian charcoal-burner, never sent on a paid embassy; the name comes from μαρίλη, charcoal dust.

head: Μαρψίης
text: Ionic form of Μαρψίας: Marpsias, an Athenian speaker mocked in Acharnians as a quarrelsome talker.

head: Μασίστρας
text: Masistras, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Μασίστρης
text: Masistres, a Persian commander named in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Μασυντίας
text: Masyntias, a slave of Philocleon in Wasps.

head: Μέγαρος
text: Megara (Μέγαρα), the Dorian city between Athens and Corinth, an enemy of Athens in the Peloponnesian War.

head: Μέγης
text: Meges, son of Phyleus, who led the men of Dulichium and the Echinades to Troy.

head: Μέλητος
text: Meletus, an Athenian poet of tragedies and drinking songs mocked by Aristophanes; perhaps the man who later prosecuted Socrates.

head: Μέμφις
text: Memphis, the old capital of Egypt on the Nile.

head: Μένιππος
text: Menippus, an Athenian nicknamed "the Swallow" in Birds.

head: Μέτων
text: Meton, the Athenian astronomer who devised a calendar cycle; in Birds he comes to survey the air for the new city and is beaten off.

head: Μεγάβαζος
text: Megabazus, a Persian noble name; in Birds 'the Dariuses and Megabazuses' stand for the kings and lords of Persia.

head: Μεγάραδε
text: to Megara, the city between Athens and Corinth.

head: Μεγάρη
text: Ionic form of Μεγάρα: Megara, daughter of Creon of Thebes and wife of Heracles. In Euripides' Heracles she and her sons wait for death under Lycus, then die by Heracles' own hand.

head: Μεγαβάτης
text: Megabates, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians; in the closing lament Xerxes is asked about the son of Megabates.

head: Μεγαίνετος
text: Megaenetus, an Athenian whom Euripides in Frogs names, with Phormisius, as a pupil of Aeschylus: a rough, warlike type.

head: Μελάνθιος
text: Melanthius, an Athenian tragic poet attacked by the comic poets, Aristophanes in Peace among them, for his harsh voice.

head: Μελανίππη
text: Melanippe, daughter of Aeolus. In Thesmophoriazusae the women charge Euripides with writing Melanippes and Phaedras, wicked women.

head: Μελησίης
text: Melesias, a man's name given as an example in Clouds; the son of Thucydides bore it.

head: Μελίτη
text: Melite, a deme inside the city of Athens.

head: Μελιστίχη
text: Melistiche, wife of Smicythion, one of the women in Ecclesiazusae hurrying to the assembly in men's shoes.

head: Μενοικεύς
text: Menoeceus. 1. A Theban, father of Creon and Jocasta; ὁ Μενοικέως, Creon. 2. Creon's son, who kills himself to save Thebes when Teiresias says the city needs his death.

head: Μερόπη
text: Merope, the Dorian wife of Polybus, king of Corinth, who raised Oedipus as her own son.

head: Μεσσάπιος
text: of Messapium, a mountain on the Boeotian coast facing Euboea; one of the beacon stations in Agamemnon.

head: Μεσσήνη
text: Messene, the old name of Messenia, the south-west Peloponnese. In Lysistrata it recalls the Messenian revolt against Sparta, when Athens sent help.

head: Μηκιστεύς
text: Mecisteus, son of Talaus and brother of Adrastus, king of Argos; father of Euryalus, who led ships to Troy.

head: Μητρογαθής
text: Metrogathes, a Lydian commander in the host of Xerxes in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Μίκα
text: Mica, one of the women at the festival in Thesmophoriazusae, whose 'baby' turns out to be a wineskin.

head: Μιλτιάδης
text: Miltiades, the Athenian general who won the battle of Marathon in 490 BC; Knights pairs him with Aristides as a man of the good old days.

head: Μολοττικός
text: Molossian, of the Molossians of Epirus, known for their large hunting dogs.

head: Μούνιχος
text: Munichus, the hero who gave his name to Munychia, the harbour hill of Athens; Μουνίχου ἀκταί, the shores of Munychia.

head: Μουσαῖος
text: Musaeus, a legendary poet and seer of early Athens, pupil or kin of Orpheus, to whom oracles and cures were credited.

head: Μύρριον
text: Myrrhion, a pet name for Myrrhine, which Cinesias uses for his wife in Lysistrata.

head: Μυγδών
text: Mygdon, a Phrygian king; in Rhesus his son Coroebus keeps the first watch for the Trojans.

head: Μυκηναῖος
text: of Mycenae, the ancient city of the Argolid where Agamemnon ruled; Mycenaean. οἱ Μυκηναῖοι, the people of Mycenae.

head: Μυκηνίς
text: Mycenaean, of Mycenae, Agamemnon's city in the Argolid; αἱ Μυκηνίδες, the women of Mycenae.

head: Μυρμιδόνες
text: the Myrmidons, the people of Phthia in Thessaly whom Achilles led to Troy; their name was said to come from μύρμηξ, ant.

head: Μυρμιδών
text: Myrmidon, son of Zeus and ancestor of the Myrmidons of Phthia in Thessaly. οἱ Μυρμιδόνες, the Myrmidons, Achilles' people, whom he leads to Troy.

head: Μυρρινίδιον
text: little Myrrhine, a pet form of Μυρρίνη: Myrrhine, the wife Cinesias begs to come home in Lysistrata.

head: Μυρτίη
text: Ionic form of Μυρτία: Myrtia, a bread-seller in Wasps, daughter of Ancylion and Sostrate, whose loaves Philocleon knocks over.

head: Μυρτίλος
text: Myrtilus, son of Hermes and charioteer of Oenomaus. Pelops won Hippodameia with his help, then threw him into the sea; dying, he cursed the house of Pelops.

head: Μυρωνίδης
text: Myronides, the Athenian general who beat the Corinthians near Megara in 457 BC with the old and young men left at home; for Aristophanes a hero of the good old days.

head: Ναύσων
text: Nauson ("ship-man"), a made-up name in Knights: a ship speaks of herself as Nauphante, daughter of Nauson.

head: Ναυφάντη
text: Nauphante, daughter of Nauson, a ship's name in Knights: the triremes refuse to sail for Hyperbolus.

head: Ναυπάκτιος
text: of Naupactus, the harbour town on the north shore of the Corinthian gulf.

head: Ναυπλιεύς
text: of Nauplia, the port of Argos; in Orestes Menelaus anchors his ships in the Nauplian harbour.

head: Ναυσικύδης
text: Nausicydes, a rich Athenian grain dealer. In Ecclesiazusae Blepyrus jokes that grain dealers should have to give grain to the poor so that Nausicydes would be of some use to them.

head: Νέμειον
text: Nemean, of Nemea, the valley near Cleonae where Heracles killed the lion; ὁ Νέμειος θήρ, the Nemean lion.

head: Νέμειος
text: Nemean, of Nemea in the Argolid, where Heracles killed the lion.

head: Νέσσος
text: Nessus, the centaur who carried Deianeira across the river Evenus and was shot by Heracles. Dying, he gave her his blood as a love charm; it later killed Heracles.

head: Νειλῶτις
text: of the Nile; ἡ Νειλῶτις χθών, the triangle of land at the Nile's mouths, the Delta, where Io's line will settle.

head: Νεμεῖος
text: of Nemea, the valley in Argolis where Heracles killed the Nemean lion.

head: Νεοκλείδης
text: Neoclides, an Athenian politician of the 390s BC, mocked by Aristophanes as blear-eyed and a thief.

head: Νίκαρχος
text: Nicarchus, an Athenian informer in Acharnians, who denounces the Boeotian's goods and is packed up and shipped off as merchandise.

head: Νῖσος
text: Nisus, king of Megara, whose life hung on a purple lock of hair; his daughter Scylla cut it off for love of Minos, and Megara fell.

head: Νικίας
text: Nicias, son of Niceratus, the rich and cautious Athenian general of the Peloponnesian War, who made the peace of 421 BC and died in Sicily in 413.

head: Νικόμαχος
text: Nicomachus, an Athenian official whom Pluto summons to Hades at the end of Frogs.

head: Νικόστρατος
text: Nicostratus of Scambonidae, an Athenian in the audience whose guess at the old man's madness Xanthias reports in Wasps.

head: Νικοδίκη
text: Nicodice, one of the old women of the chorus in Lysistrata, hurrying with water to save the women on the Acropolis.

head: Νιόβη
text: Niobe, daughter of Tantalus and wife of Amphion of Thebes. She boasted that she had more children than Leto, so Apollo and Artemis killed them all; she wept until she turned to stone on Mount Sipylus.

head: Νιρεύς
text: Nireus of Syme, the handsomest of the Greeks at Troy after Achilles, though a poor fighter.

head: Νυσαῖοι
text: of Nysa, the mountain where Dionysus was reared; Νυσαῖα ὄρη, the Nysaean mountains.

head: Νυσαῖος
text: Nysaean, of Nysa, the mountain where nymphs reared the infant Dionysus; the Greeks placed it in many lands.

head: Οἴαγρος
text: Oeagrus, an Athenian tragic actor, famous as Niobe.

head: Οἰβάρης
text: Oebares, a Persian noble lost in the war, named in the lament of Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Οἰδιπόδης
text: Another form of Οἰδίπους: Oedipus, son of Laius and Jocasta, king of Thebes. He killed his father and married his mother without knowing them, and blinded himself when he learned the truth.

head: Οἰκλείδης
text: son of Oecles: Amphiaraus, the seer of Argos, one of the Seven against Thebes.

head: Οἰκλῆς
text: Oecles, son of Antiphates, of Argos, father of the seer Amphiaraus.

head: Οἰνεΐδης
text: son or grandson of Oeneus (Οἰνεύς), king of Calydon; in Rhesus it is Diomedes, who with Odysseus killed Rhesus.

head: Οἰνεύς
text: Oeneus, king of Calydon in Aetolia, father of Tydeus, Meleager, and Deianeira. Euripides made him the ruined hero of a lost play; in Acharnians Euripides offers his rags to Dicaeopolis, who rejects them.

head: Οἰνιάδη
text: Oeniadae, a town in Acarnania near the mouth of the Achelous; the river god Achelous comes from there to fight Heracles in Trachiniae.

head: Οἰνόμαος
text: Oenomaus, king of Pisa in Elis and father of Hippodamia. He made her suitors race him in chariots and killed those he beat, until Pelops won by bribing his charioteer Myrtilus.

head: Οἰνωᾶτις
text: Oenoatis, a title of Artemis, from her shrine at Oenoe in Argolis.

head: Οἰώνιχος
text: Oeonichus, an Athenian named in Knights as the companion of the lewd Ariphrades.

head: Πάγγαιον
text: Pangaeum, a mountain range in Thrace near the Strymon, rich in gold and silver mines.

head: Πάνδροσος
text: Pandrosos, daughter of Cecrops, worshipped at Athens beside Athena; the women swear by her in Lysistrata.

head: Πάρις
text: Paris, also called Alexander, son of Priam and Hecuba. He carried off Helen from Menelaus at Sparta and so caused the Trojan War.

head: Πάρθος
text: Parthus, a Persian lost at Salamis, mourned in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Παγγαῖον
text: Pangaeum, a mountain of gold and silver mines in Thrace near the Strymon; in Rhesus the dead Rhesus, made a god, will dwell in its caves.

head: Παιονίδης
text: a man of Paeonidae, a deme of Attica; so Cinesias names himself in Lysistrata.

head: Πακτωλός
text: Pactolus, a river of Lydia flowing past Sardis, known for its gold.

head: Παλλαντίδης
text: son of Pallas: the Pallantidae, Theseus' cousins, whom he killed; he went into exile at Troezen for it.

head: Παλληνεύς
text: of Pallene, an Attic deme with a shrine of Athena; in Children of Heracles the battle is fought near it.

head: Πανθοΐδης
text: son of Panthous, a Trojan elder whose sons were Euphorbus, Polydamas, and Hyperenor.

head: Παντακλέης
text: Ionic form of Παντακλῆς: Pantacles, an Athenian called in Frogs the clumsiest of men, who put on his helmet before fixing its crest.

head: Παρδόκης
text: Pardocas, one of the slaves or Scythian archers whom Aeacus calls out to seize Dionysus' slave in Frogs.

head: Παρνάσιος
text: of Parnassus, the mountain above Delphi, sacred to Apollo and Dionysus; Parnassian.

head: Παρνάσσιος
text: of Parnassus, the mountain above Delphi.

head: Παρνασιάς
text: of Parnassus, the mountain above Delphi; αἱ Παρνασιάδες κορυφαί, the peaks of Parnassus.

head: Παρνασσός
text: Parnassus, the mountain in Phocis above Delphi, sacred to Apollo, Dionysus, and the Muses.

head: Παρνήσιος
text: of Mount Parnes, the range on the northern border of Attica; ἄνθρακες Παρνήσιοι, charcoal from Parnes.

head: Παρθενοπαῖος
text: Parthenopaeus, son of Atalanta, an Arcadian, one of the Seven who marched against Thebes.

head: Παρράσιος
text: Parrhasian, of Parrhasia in southwest Arcadia; Apollo sends Orestes to live a year on Parrhasian soil.

head: Πασίης
text: Pasias, an Athenian to whom Strepsiades owes twelve minae in Clouds.

head: Πατροκλέης
text: Ionic form of Πατροκλῆς: Patrocles, a stingy rich Athenian in Wealth who has not bathed since the day he was born.

head: Πατροκλείδης
text: Patrocleides, an Athenian whom Birds mocks for soiling himself.

head: Πείσανδρος
text: Peisander, an Athenian politician mocked by Aristophanes as a coward; in 411 BC he was a leader of the oligarchic coup of the Four Hundred.

head: Πειρηναῖος
text: of Peirene, the spring at Corinth where Bellerophon caught Pegasus; Πειρηναῖος πῶλος, Pegasus.

head: Πεισίης
text: Ionic form of Πεισίας: Pisias; ὁ Πεισίου, the son of Pisias, an Athenian mocked in Birds as a traitor ready to open the gates.

head: Πελαργικός
text: of storks (πελαργός), Aristophanes' pun on the old Pelasgic wall of the Athenian Acropolis. τὸ Πελαργικόν, the Stork Wall, the citadel of Cloudcuckooland in Birds.

head: Πελλάνη
text: Doric Πελλάνα for Πελλήνη: Pellene, a town of Achaea; the Spartan herald in Lysistrata uses the name for a pun on the woman he wants.

head: Πελλήνη
text: Pellene, the easternmost of the twelve Achaean cities, near Sicyon.

head: Πελοπίδης
text: son or descendant of Pelops (Πέλοψ): used of Atreus' line, Agamemnon and Menelaus, and of Orestes. οἱ Πελοπίδαι, the house of Pelops.

head: Πελοπίη
text: Ionic form of Πελοπία, feminine of Πελόπιος: of Pelops; ἡ Πελοπία χώρα or αἶα, the land of Pelops, the Peloponnese.

head: Πελοποννήσιοι
text: the Peloponnesians, the people of the Peloponnese, the great southern peninsula of Greece; in Aristophanes, Sparta and her allies, Athens' enemies in the war.

head: Πελοποννήσιος
text: of the Peloponnese, the southern peninsula of Greece; Peloponnesian. οἱ Πελοποννήσιοι, Sparta and her allies, Athens' enemies in the war of Aristophanes' day.

head: Πενθεύς
text: Pentheus, son of Echion and Agave, Cadmus' daughter, and king of Thebes after Cadmus. He fights the worship of Dionysus, and his mother and the Bacchants tear him apart.

head: Πεπάρηθος
text: Peparethus, an island of the Aegean off Thessaly, known for its wine.

head: Περγασῆσι
text: at Pergase, an Attic deme.

head: Περικλείδης
text: Pericleidas (Περικλείδας), a Spartan who came to Athens as a suppliant to beg help against the Messenian revolt, as Lysistrata reminds the Spartans.

head: Περικλύμενος
text: Periclymenus, son of Poseidon, a Theban defender who kills Parthenopaeus with a stone thrown from the wall.

head: Περραιβός
text: Perrhaebian. οἱ Περραιβοί, the Perrhaebians, a people of northern Thessaly at the foot of Mount Olympus, whose land the king of Argos claims as his border.

head: Περσεφόνεια
text: a poetic form of Περσεφόνη: Persephone, daughter of Zeus and Demeter and queen of the dead.

head: Περσονόμος
text: of Persian rule. In Persians the chorus mourns the honour of Persia's rule.

head: Πηγάσειος
text: of Pegasus, the winged horse; in Peace Trygaeus hails his dung-beetle as his Pegasus.

head: Πηγασταγών
text: Pegastagon, an Egyptian-born commander in Xerxes' army, named in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Πηλιακός
text: of Pelion, the wooded mountain of Magnesia in Thessaly; the plays use the feminine Πηλιάς: πεῦκαι Πηλιάδες, pine torches from Pelion.

head: Πηλιῶτις
text: of Pelion, the wooded mountain of Magnesia in Thessaly; ἡ Πηλιῶτις Ἰωλκός, Iolcus below Pelion.

head: Πηνειός
text: Peneus, the chief river of Thessaly, which flows out to the sea through the vale of Tempe between Olympus and Ossa; also its god.

head: Πίνδος
text: Pindus, the long mountain range of northern Greece between Thessaly and Epirus.

head: Πίτταλος
text: Pittalus, an Athenian doctor of Aristophanes' day; to go to Pittalus' house is to go to the doctor.

head: Πιερίδες
text: the Pierides, the Muses, named from Pieria near Mount Olympus, where they were first worshipped.

head: Πιερίς
text: Pierian, of Pieria, the land at the foot of Olympus, home of the Muses. αἱ Πιερίδες, the Muses.

head: Πισάτης
text: Pisatan, of Pisa, the old city near Olympia ruled by Oenomaus; the Pisatan maiden is Hippodameia.

head: Πισᾶτις
text: of Pisa, the old city near Olympia; ἡ Πισᾶτις παρθένος, Hippodamia, whom Pelops won.

head: Πισθέταιρος
text: Peisthetaerus ("persuader of his friend"), the Athenian who leaves Athens with Euelpides and talks the birds into building Cloudcuckooland in Aristophanes' Birds.

head: Πιτθεύς
text: Pittheus, son of Pelops, king of Troezen, father of Aethra, and grandfather of Theseus, whom he raised. In Hippolytus he has brought up Hippolytus too.

head: Πλαθάνη
text: Plathane, the innkeeper's partner in Aristophanes' Frogs, called out to help accuse Dionysus, dressed as Heracles, of eating them out of house and home.

head: Πλαταιεῖς
text: the Plataeans, people of Plataea in Boeotia, Athens' old allies, who were given Athenian citizenship; Frogs uses them as the model for freeing the slaves who fought at Arginusae.

head: Πλαταιός
text: a Plataean, of Plataea in Boeotia, Athens' old ally whose people were made Athenian citizens; in Frogs slaves who fought in one sea battle become Plataeans.

head: Πλεισθένης
text: Pleisthenes, son of Atreus and in some stories the father of Agamemnon and Menelaus; the house of Pleisthenes is Agamemnon's.

head: Πλεισθενίδης
text: son or descendant of Pleisthenes (Πλεισθένης), son of Atreus; οἱ Πλεισθενίδαι, the house of Atreus.

head: Πόλυβος
text: Polybus, king of Corinth, who raised Oedipus as his own son; Oedipus believes him to be his father.

head: Πολυφόντης
text: Polyphontes, a Theban champion who faces Capaneus at the Electran gate in Seven against Thebes.

head: Πολυμήστωρ
text: Polymestor, king of the Thracians of the Chersonese. In Hecuba he murders Polydorus, Priam's son left in his care, for his gold; Hecuba blinds him and kills his sons.

head: Πολυχαρείδας
text: Polycharidas, a Spartan form of address in Lysistrata, read either as a name or as a friendly greeting, "dear friend".

head: Πραξαγόρη
text: Praxagora ("active in the assembly"), the Athenian woman who leads the women's takeover of the assembly in Aristophanes' Assemblywomen.

head: Πρέπις
text: Prepis, an Athenian of Aristophanes' day, mocked in Acharnians for his wide arse.

head: Πριαμίδης
text: son of Priam (Πρίαμος), king of Troy: used of Hector, Paris, Helenus, Polydorus, and his other sons. οἱ Πριαμίδαι, Priam's sons.

head: Πριαμίς
text: of Priam, king of Troy: Πριαμὶς γῆ, Priam's land, Troy; Πριαμίδες πύλαι, the gates of Priam's house.

head: Πριαμικός
text: of Priam (Πρίαμος), king of Troy; Trojan.

head: Πρινίδης
text: Prinides ("oak-son"), a poor Acharnian named in Acharnians as one who never went on embassies.

head: Πρόκνη
text: Procne, daughter of Pandion, king of Athens, and wife of Tereus. She killed her son Itys to punish Tereus and became a bird; in Birds she is the nightingale, the Hoopoe's mate.

head: Προξενίδης
text: Proxenides, of the made-up deme Kompos ("Braggart"), an Athenian whom Aristophanes mocks as a boaster.

head: Προῖτος
text: Proetus, a Theban after whom the Proetid gate of Thebes was named; Tydeus attacks this gate in Seven against Thebes.

head: Προκρούστης
text: Procrustes ('the stretcher'), a robber who made travellers fit his bed, stretching or cutting them; Theseus killed him. In Assemblywomen the young man fears the same fate.

head: Προνάπης
text: Pronapes, an Athenian, father of Amynias in Wasps.

head: Προναίη
text: Ionic form of Προναία: Pronaea ("before the temple"), a title of Athena at Delphi, whose chapel stood in front of the temple of Apollo.

head: Πύλιος
text: Pylian, of Pylos, the city of Nestor in the western Peloponnese; ὁ Πύλιος, Nestor.

head: Πύρρανδρος
text: Pyrrhandrus, an Athenian named in Knights for a scheme credited to him; nothing else is known of him.

head: Πυλάδης
text: Pylades, son of Strophius, king of Phocis. Raised with Orestes and his friend for life; he helps him avenge Agamemnon and later marries Electra.

head: Πυθάγγελος
