text: Pythangelus, an Athenian tragic poet named in Frogs as one not worth bringing back.

head: Θάρυβις
text: Tharybis, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, lost at Salamis.

head: Θαρραλείδης
text: Tharrelides, an Athenian name used in a joke in Birds: Euelpides calls his jackdaw “son of Tharrelides”.

head: Θαρρελείδης
text: Tharreleides, in Birds the jackdaw is called "son of Tharreleides", a joke on an Athenian name.

head: Θέογνις
text: Theognis, a tragic poet of Aristophanes' day, mocked for his dull, cold plays.

head: Θεμίσκυρα
text: Themiscyra, the plain on the south coast of the Black Sea by the river Thermodon, home of the Amazons.

head: Θεμιστοκλέης
text: Themistocles, the Athenian leader who built the fleet and won the battle of Salamis (480 BC). In Knights Aristophanes recalls that he was said to have died by drinking bull's blood.

head: Θεμιστοκλῆς
text: Themistocles, the Athenian statesman who built the fleet and won at Salamis in 480 BC; later exiled, he was said to have died by drinking bull's blood.

head: Θεόφραστος
text: Theophrastus (Θούφραστος in the play), an Athenian of the smart set around Phrynichus, at the party Philocleon wrecks in Wasps.

head: Θεοκλύμενος
text: Theoclymenus, son of Proteus and king of Egypt in Euripides' Helen. He wants to marry Helen, who tricks him and escapes with Menelaus.

head: Θεονόη
text: Theonoe, daughter of Proteus, king of Egypt, and sister of Theoclymenus. A prophetess who knows the gods' will, she keeps Menelaus' secret and helps him and Helen escape in Euripides' Helen.

head: Θερμώδων
text: Thermodon, a river of Pontus on the Black Sea, the home of the Amazons.

head: Θερσίτης
text: Thersites, the ugliest and most foul-mouthed of the Greeks at Troy, beaten by Odysseus for railing at Agamemnon.

head: Θεσμοφόρειον
text: the Thesmophorion, the temple of Demeter and Persephone, the Two Goddesses, where Athenian women kept the Thesmophoria; the setting of Aristophanes' Thesmophoriazusae.

head: Θεσπρωτός
text: Thesprotian, of Thesprotia in Epirus, the land of the oracle of Zeus at Dodona.

head: Θεστιάς
text: daughter of Thestius (Θέστιος): Leda, mother of Helen and Clytemnestra, or Althaea, mother of Meleager.

head: Θεστορεῖος
text: son of Thestor (Θέστωρ): Calchas, the Greek prophet at Troy.

head: Θήβη
text: Thebes, the chief city of Boeotia, founded by Cadmus; the city of Oedipus, Pentheus, and the Seven against Thebes.

head: Θήβηθεν
text: from Thebes (Θήβη), the chief city of Boeotia.

head: Θηβαῖος
text: Theban, of Thebes in Boeotia, the city of Cadmus and Dionysus; οἱ Θηβαῖοι, the Thebans. In the opening of Andromache it refers instead to Thebe in the Troad, Andromache’s home.

head: Θηβαιγενής
text: born of Thebes, Theban.

head: Θορίκιος
text: Thorician; in Oedipus at Colonus, the name of a rock near the place where Oedipus dies. Its link to Thoricus, a deme on the south-east coast of Attica, is uncertain.

head: Θούμαντις
text: Thumantis, a poor Athenian, homeless and hungry, mocked in Knights.

head: Θουφάνης
text: Thuphanes, a clerk and follower of Cleon whom Demos in Knights blames for cheating him.

head: Θουκυδίδης
text: Thucydides, son of Melesias, the Athenian statesman who led the opposition to Pericles; in Acharnians and Wasps he is an old man beaten in court by young speakers.

head: Θρῄκιος
text: poetic form of Θρᾴκιος: Thracian, of Thrace, the wild land north of the Aegean. Θρῄκιαι πνοαί, the north winds that blow from Thrace.

head: Θρονιάς
text: of Thronium, the chief town of the eastern Locrians, home of Ajax son of Oileus.

head: Θυμαιτίς
text: Thymaetian, of the Attic deme of the Thymaetadae; a σισύρα Θυμαιτίς, a rough cloak of the kind made there.

head: Θυμβραῖος
text: of Thymbra in the Troad; a title of Apollo, who had a temple there.

head: Θωρυκίων
text: Thorycion, an Athenian tax collector at Aegina, cursed in Frogs as a traitor who smuggled forbidden goods to the enemy.

head: Ρ(ῆσος
text: Rhesus, king of Thrace and ally of the Trojans, famed for his snow-white horses. Odysseus and Diomedes kill him in his sleep on his first night at Troy.

head: Σάκας
text: Sacas, the nickname of Acestor, a tragic poet at Athens in Aristophanes' time, so called for his foreign birth; Birds names him at the start.

head: Σαΐος
text: Saian: the Saii, a Thracian tribe; in Peace a boy sings the line on the Saian who now enjoys the shield its owner left in a bush.

head: Σαλαβακχώ
text: Salabaccho, an Athenian prostitute of Aristophanes' day, named with Cynna in Knights as a byword for vileness.

head: Σαλμυδήσσιος
text: of Salmydessus, a stretch of the Thracian coast on the Black Sea, hostile to ships.

head: Σαλμυδησσός
text: Salmydessus, a stretch of the Thracian coast on the Black Sea north-west of the Bosporus, home of king Phineus.

head: Σαρδανάπαλλος
text: Sardanapallus, the last king of Assyria, a byword for luxury; in Birds Peisetaerus calls an overdressed Athenian official by his name.

head: Σαρπηδόνιος
text: of Sarpedon; τὸ Σαρπηδόνιον χῶμα, the sandy mound of Sarpedon, a cape on the coast of Cilicia.

head: Σαρωνικός
text: Saronic, of the Saronic Gulf, the sea between Attica and the Argolid, with Salamis and Aegina in it.

head: Σέλλος
text: Sellus, named in Wasps as father of the braggart Aeschines and of Amynias, both mocked by Aristophanes.

head: Σεβῖνος
text: Sebinus, a made-up name built on an obscene verb; 'Sebinus of Anaphlystus' makes a sexual joke in Frogs and Ecclesiazusae.

head: Σεισάμης
text: Seisames the Mysian, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, killed at Salamis.

head: Σελλάρτιος
text: Sellartius, in Wasps a mock name for the father of Aeschines, a braggart.

head: Σερίφιος
text: of Seriphos, a small, poor island of the Cyclades.

head: Σευάλκης
text: Seualces, a Persian lord named among the lost in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Σφήττιος
text: of Sphettus, an Attic deme; the deme of Chaerephon, the friend of Socrates. Wealth also mentions Sphettian vinegar.

head: Σίγειον
text: Sigeum, a headland of the Troad at the mouth of the Hellespont, where the Greeks drew up their ships.

head: Σίπυλος
text: Sipylus, a mountain of Lydia, where Niobe was turned to stone.

head: Σιβύρτιος
text: Sibyrtius, named in Acharnians as father of Cleisthenes, the effeminate Athenian Aristophanes mocks.

head: Σιληνιαί
text: of the Silenian shore, a rocky coast of Salamis where a Persian commander fell.

head: Σιμαίθα
text: Simaetha, a Megarian courtesan; in Acharnians Dicaeopolis says young Athenians stole her and so began the war.

head: Σιμοεντιάς
text: of the Simois, the river of the Trojan plain that joins the Scamander.

head: Σιμουντίς
text: of the Simois, the river of Troy that joins the Scamander below the city; hence Trojan.

head: Σισύφειον
text: of Sisyphus, the cunning king of Corinth punished in Hades with a stone; Σισύφειος πέτρος, Sisyphus' stone. τὸ Σισύφειον σπέρμα, 'Sisyphus' seed', is a sneer at Odysseus, said to be his son.

head: Σισύφειος
text: of Sisyphus, the cunning king of Corinth punished in Hades with a rolling stone; hence Corinthian. 'The seed of Sisyphus' is Odysseus, said to be his son.

head: Σισυφίδης
text: son of Sisyphus (Σίσυφος): Odysseus, in the slur that Sisyphus, not Laertes, was his father.

head: Σκαμάνδριος
text: of the Scamander, the river in the plain of Troy; hence Trojan.

head: Σκαμβωνίδης
text: of the Attic deme Scambonidae, within the city of Athens; Nicostratus of Scambonidae guesses at the old man's disease in Wasps.

head: Σκεβλύας
text: Sceblyas, one of the slaves Aeacus calls in Frogs, with Ditylas and Pardocas, to seize Xanthias.

head: Σκελλίας
text: Scellias, an Athenian, father of the oligarch Aristocrates; in Birds Euelpides says he loathes "the son of Scellias".

head: Σκιώνη
text: Scione, a town of Pallene in Chalcidice that revolted from Athens in 423 BC and was besieged.

head: Σμίκυθος
text: Smicythus, a man's name the disguised women of Assemblywomen use for one another on their way to the assembly.

head: Σμικύθη
text: Smicythes, an Athenian whom Knights gives a woman's name ending, mocking him as womanish.

head: Σμικυθίων
text: Smicythion, an Athenian man's name: in Wasps one of the old jurors, in Assemblywomen the husband of Melistiche.

head: Σμοῖος
text: Smoeus, an Athenian mocked in Ecclesiazusae, who in a horseman's dress licks clean the women's dishes, a sexual joke.

head: Σοσθάνης
text: Sosthanes, a Persian charioteer in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Σοῦσος
text: Susa (Σοῦσα), the royal city of the Persian kings in Susiana, from which Xerxes' army set out in Aeschylus' Persians.

head: Σουνιέρακος
text: Sunium-hawk, a joke title in Birds blending Poseidon of Sunium with a hawk.

head: Σουσίς
text: of Susa, the Persian royal city; ἄστυ Σουσίδος, the city of Susa.

head: Σουσισκάνης
text: Susiscanes, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, sent by Egypt and the Nile, and later mourned among the lost.

head: Σπαρτιάτης
text: Spartiate, a full citizen of Sparta; a Spartan.

head: Σπερχειός
text: Spercheius, a river of southern Thessaly flowing into the Malian Gulf, and its river god.

head: Σπίνθαρος
text: Spintharus of Heracleia on the Black Sea, a tragic poet of Aristophanes' day, mocked in Birds as a barbarian and a Phrygian.

head: Σποργίλος
text: Sporgilus, an Athenian barber mocked in Birds.

head: Σθένελος
text: Sthenelus, son of Perseus and father of Eurystheus. Another Sthenelus, son of Capaneus, leads Argive ships to Troy; Aristophanes also names a tragic actor Sthenelus.

head: Σθενέβοια
text: Stheneboea, wife of Proetus, who loved Bellerophon and killed herself; in Frogs Aeschylus cites Euripides' play about her as one that showed bad women.

head: Στιλβίδης
text: Stilbides, a well-known Athenian seer; in Peace Trygaeus jokes at his expense while preparing a sacrifice without a seer’s help.

head: Στιλβωνίδης
text: Stilbonides ('son of Shiny'), a made-up name in Birds: an imagined father of a pretty boy hails the speaker as Stilbonides.

head: Στρατονίκη
text: Stratonice ('army victory'), a woman's name the chorus of Thesmophoriazusae sets against the men.

head: Στρατυλλίς
text: Stratyllis, the leader of the old women's chorus in Lysistrata.

head: Στρεψιάδης
text: Strepsiades ("twister"), son of Phidon, of the deme Cicynna, the indebted old farmer of Aristophanes' Clouds who enrols at Socrates' school to learn how to cheat his creditors.

head: Στρούθιος
text: Sparrowite, a mock deme name for Philocrates the bird-seller in Birds, from στρουθός, sparrow.

head: Στρυμόδωρος
text: Strymodorus, a name Aristophanes gives to old Athenians: an Acharnian whose slave girl steals wood, and one of the old jurors of Wasps.

head: Συβαρῖτις
text: a Sybarite woman, of Sybaris, the rich Greek city of southern Italy, famed for luxury; Sybarite fables were short and funny.

head: Συέννεσις
text: Syennesis, a common name of the kings of Cilicia; in Persians a Syennesis leads the Cilicians and dies at Salamis.

head: Συρακόσιος
text: Syracosius, an Athenian politician, named in Birds as the Jay for his chatter. As an adjective, Syracusan, of Syracuse in Sicily.

head: Σωκρατίδιον
text: little Socrates, dear Socrates: Strepsiades' coaxing pet name for Socrates in Clouds.

head: Σωσίης
text: Sosias, a common slave name; one of the two slaves guarding Philocleon at the start of Aristophanes' Wasps.

head: Σωστράτη
text: Sostrate, a common Athenian woman's name: Clouds uses it in a joke about the names of women, and a Sostrate comes to the women's meeting in Assemblywomen.

head: Ταλθύβιος
text: Talthybius, the herald of Agamemnon at Troy. In Euripides he brings the captive Trojan women the Greeks' orders and news of their deaths.

head: Ταρτήσιος
text: variant spelling of Ταρτήσσιος: of Tartessus, a district in the south of Spain beyond the Pillars of Heracles; Tartessian.

head: Ταρτήσσιος
text: of Tartessus, a district in the south of Spain beyond the Pillars of Heracles; Tartessian. In Frogs Aeacus threatens Dionysus with a Tartessian lamprey.

head: Τέκμησσα
text: Tecmessa, daughter of the Phrygian king Teleutas, taken captive by the Greeks and given to Ajax, who lived with her as his wife; mother of his son Eurysaces.

head: Τειθράσιος
text: of Teithras, an Attic deme; in Frogs the Gorgons of Teithras.

head: Τειρεσίης
text: Ionic form of Τειρεσίας: Teiresias, the blind prophet of Thebes, who lived to a great age. He warns Oedipus, Creon, and Pentheus, and none of them heeds him in time.

head: Τεισαμενοφαίνιππος
text: Tisamenus-Phaenippuses, a joke compound of two names in Acharnians, for Athenians who draw pay on embassies far away.

head: Τεισιάδης
text: Teisiades, one of the old jurors in Wasps.

head: Τενάγων
text: Tenagon, the best of the Bactrians, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, killed at Salamis.

head: Τεύθρας
text: Teuthras, an early king of Mysia who brought up Telephus; the city of Teuthras is in Mysia.

head: Τεῦκρος
text: Teucer, son of Telamon and Hesione, half-brother of Ajax, and the best archer among the Greeks at Troy. In Ajax he fights for his dead brother's right to burial.

head: Τευκρίς
text: Teucrian, of Teucer, the first king of Troy; ἡ Τευκρὶς αἶα, Troy.

head: Τευμησσός
text: Teumessus, a village and hill in the plain of Thebes.

head: Τήλεφος
text: Telephus, son of Heracles and Auge, king of Mysia, wounded by Achilles and healed by his spear. Euripides showed him as a king in a beggar's rags, a play Aristophanes mocks in Acharnians.

head: Τήνιος
text: of Tenos, an island of the Cyclades near Delos; in Wealth the doctor's paste uses three heads of Tenian garlic.

head: Τήρεια
text: of Tereus (Τηρεύς), the Thracian king; his wife Procne, turned into a nightingale, laments her son.

head: Τηρεύς
text: Tereus, a Thracian king who married Procne, daughter of Pandion of Athens, and raped her sister Philomela; the gods turned him into a hoopoe. In Birds, Tereus the hoopoe is the bird king the two Athenians seek out.

head: Τίρυνς
text: Tiryns, an ancient city of the Argolid near Argos, famous for its huge walls; Heracles' home, where Alcmene lives in Women of Trachis.

head: Τιμόκλεια
text: Timocleia, the woman who presides over the women's assembly in Thesmophoriazusae.

head: Τιμόθεος
text: Timotheus, son of Conon, Athenian general of the fourth century BC; Wealth mentions his tower as a sign of riches.

head: Τιρύνθιος
text: of Tiryns, the ancient city south-east of Argos; Tirynthian. In Alcestis Eurystheus, Heracles' master, and Alcmene, his mother, are both Tirynthian.

head: Τληπόλεμος
text: Tlepolemus, son of Heracles, who killed his great-uncle Licymnius; in Clouds the injured creditor groans in words from a tragedy about Licymnius’ death.

head: Τόλμος
text: Tolmus, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, mourned among the dead.

head: Τριβαλλός
text: a Triballian, one of the Triballi, a Thracian people; in Birds the Triballian is a barbarian god in heaven's embassy who speaks broken Greek.

head: Τρικορυσίος
text: of Tricorythus, an Attic deme near Marathon; in Lysistrata a gnat comes from there.

head: Τροίαθεν
text: from Troy (Τροία); also Ionic Τροίηθεν.

head: Τροιζήνιος
text: of Troezen, the city in the south-east of the Argolid where Pittheus ruled; Troezenian.

head: Τροζήνιος
text: of Troezen, a city on the Argolid coast facing Athens, where Theseus was born and where Hippolytus is set; Troezenian.

head: Τρυγαῖος
text: Trygaeus ("vintager"), the farmer of Athmonon who flies to heaven on a dung beetle and brings back Peace in Aristophanes' Peace.

head: Τυνδάρειος
text: of Tyndareus, king of Sparta and husband of Leda. οἱ Τυνδάρειοι κόροι, Castor and Polydeuces; the oath of Tyndareus bound Helen's suitors to defend her marriage.

head: Τυρσηνίς
text: Tyrrhenian, of the Tyrrhenians (Etruscans) and their sea west of Italy. Jason calls Medea worse than the Tyrrhenian Scylla.

head: Χάβης
text: Chabes of Phlya, an old juror named in Wasps.

head: Χάριππος
text: Charippus, one of the horsey names Strepsiades' wife wanted for their son in Clouds.

head: Χαίρις
text: Chaeris, an Athenian piper and lyre-player mocked by Aristophanes for his bad playing.

head: Χαιρέης
text: Chaereas, an Athenian named in Wasps as the father of a lewd young man.

head: Χαιρεφῶν
text: Chaerephon of Sphettus, the friend and follower of Socrates, mocked by Aristophanes as pale and thin; in Clouds he is one of the students in Socrates' school.

head: Χαιρητάδης
text: Chaeretades, an Athenian man's name; in Assemblywomen the wife of Chaeretades comes to the women's meeting.

head: Χαιριδεύς
text: son of Chaeris (Χαῖρις), a bad piper; οἱ Χαιριδῆς, Dicaeopolis' name for the Theban's droning pipers in Acharnians.

head: Χαλκωδοντίδης
text: descendant of Chalcodon (Χαλκώδων), king of Euboea; hence Euboean.

head: Χαριξένα
text: Charixena, an early woman poet and musician; "as in Charixena's day" meant old-fashioned or silly.

head: Χαρινάδης
text: Charinades, an old Athenian juror in Wasps; in Peace a neighbour the farmers call in to drink.

head: Χαριτιμίδης
text: Charitimides, an Athenian called on by the chorus of Ecclesiazusae, with Smicythus and Draces, to hurry to the assembly.

head: Χαρμῖνος
text: Charminus, an Athenian general who lost a sea fight in 411 BC.

head: Χολλῄδης
text: of Cholleidae, a deme of Attica; Dicaeopolis of Acharnians is from there.

head: Χολοζύγης
text: Cholozyges, the magistrate's mocking name in Lysistrata for Demostratus, who urged the Sicilian expedition.

head: Χρεμύλος
text: Chremylus, the poor, honest Athenian farmer of Aristophanes' Wealth who takes the blind god Wealth home and has his sight restored.

head: Χρήμων
text: Chremon, one of the old jurors of the chorus in Wasps.

head: Χρυσεύς
text: of Chrysa; in Aeschylus' Persians the home of a commander killed at Salamis.

head: Χρυσηίς
text: Chryseis, daughter of Chryses, priest of Apollo, Agamemnon's captive at Troy; Clytemnestra mocks Agamemnon as the darling of the Chryseises.

head: Χρυσόθεμις
text: Chrysothemis, daughter of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, sister of Electra. In Sophocles' Electra she gives in to Clytemnestra and Aegisthus and will not help her sister.

head: Ψάμμις
text: Psammis, a Persian commander in Aeschylus' Persians, mourned among the dead.

head: Ψαμάθη
text: Psamathe, a Nereid, wife first of Aeacus and then of Proteus; in Helen she is the mother of Theoclymenus and Theonoe.

head: Ψευδαρτάβης
text: Pseudartabas ('false Artabas'), the comic Persian envoy in Acharnians, the King's Eye, who speaks gibberish Persian.

head: Ζακύνθιος
text: Zacynthian, of Zacynthus, an island off the west coast of the Peloponnese.

head: Ζῆθος
text: Zethus, son of Zeus and Antiope and twin brother of Amphion; the two brothers built the walls of Thebes.

head: οἰταῖος
text: of Oeta, the mountain in southern Thessaly above Trachis, where Heracles was burnt on his pyre.

head: τανταλίδης
text: son or descendant of Tantalus (Τάνταλος); in the plays the house of Atreus, Agamemnon and Menelaus and their children, who inherit the curse on Tantalus' line.
